ValidatedSettings.description:
The validated subset of the `/api/v1/setting` key/value table, as a single document keyed by the literal dotted setting names.

**Synthetic — this shape is not an endpoint's request body.** The real API writes one key at a time (`PUT /api/v1/setting/{key}` with a `SetSettingRequest` body) and stores every value as a string. This schema collects the keys that `validateSettingValue` constrains, plus the two secret keys that endpoint deliberately allows through (`hardcover.api_token`, `calibre.plugin_api_key`), so the settings singleton has one document to validate against. Property types are the semantic types the values are validated as, before they are stringified for the wire.

Derived from the `PUT /api/v1/setting/{key}` handler in the Bindery sources; every key here is validated, and unlisted keys pass through unvalidated and unchanged.

hardcover.api_token.description: Hardcover API token. A writable secret: rejected only for control characters, and never returned by GET.

hardcover.sync_interval.description: Go duration string within `[1h, 168h]`. Takes effect only after a restart.

abs.base_url.description: Audiobookshelf base URL; must pass `abs.ValidateBaseURLSecure` (SSRF-safe http/https).

calibre.library_path.description: Existing directory. Validation stats the local filesystem.

calibre.plugin_url.description: http/https URL whose host passes the outbound SSRF policy.

calibre.plugin_api_key.description: Calibre plugin API key. A writable secret, never returned by GET.

cwa.ingest_path.description: Existing directory. Validation stats the local filesystem.

import.mode.description: How imported files reach the library.

import.drop_folder.description: Existing directory. Validation stats the local filesystem.

default.media_type.description: Default media type for new items.

author.default_monitor_mode.description: Default monitoring mode for new authors (`series` is per-author only).

library.defaultRootFolderId.description: Positive integer identifying an existing root folder.

search.interval.description: Go duration string within `[1h, 168h]`. Takes effect only after a restart.

BackupFilename.name: filename
BackupFilename.description: Backup file name inside <dataDir>/backups. Validated against ^bindery_[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.db$ — it can contain no slash, backslash or dot other than the .db extension.

tags.name: abs
tags.description: Audiobookshelf (ABS) import: source configuration, live connection/library probes, asynchronous import runs with rollback, the ambiguous-match review queue, and ABS-vs-upstream metadata conflict resolution. Every route is admin-only.

tags.name: auth
tags.description:
Authentication, session, user, OIDC, and API-key management.

**Credentials.** A request authenticates either with the signed session cookie `bindery_session` (`HttpOnly`, `Path=/`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure` per `BINDERY_COOKIE_SECURE`; 12 h, or 30 days with `rememberMe`) or with the instance API key, supplied as the `X-Api-Key` header — or as a `?apikey=` query parameter, which is honoured on safe methods (GET/HEAD/OPTIONS) only. The session cookie embeds the user's `session_epoch`; bumping it (any password change or admin reset) invalidates every outstanding cookie for that user.

**CSRF.** Mutating requests that are not API-key-authenticated must carry `X-Requested-With: bindery-ui`, and — whenever a `bindery_session` cookie is present — an `X-CSRF-Token` header matching the readable `bindery_csrf` cookie issued by `GET /api/v1/auth/csrf`. Either guard failing returns `403`. Paths listed in `auth.AllowUnauthPath` are exempt from both.

**Unauthenticated routes.** `auth.AllowUnauthPath` always lets through `/api/v1/auth/status`, `/login`, `/logout`, `/setup`, `/csrf`, `GET /api/v1/auth/oidc/providers` (the `PUT` is admin-only), and any `/api/v1/auth/oidc/**/login` or `/api/v1/auth/oidc/**/callback` path. Those operations carry `security: []` here.

**Modes.** The `auth.mode` setting shifts the whole picture: `disabled` skips the check entirely, `local-only` grants admin to trusted LAN/loopback peers, and `proxy` trusts an identity header from a configured upstream.

tags.name: author
tags.description: Authors — the core library resource. CRUD, monitoring policy, aliases and merges, metadata relinking, catalogue refresh.

tags.name: backup
tags.description: SQLite database snapshots: list, create (VACUUM INTO), restore over the live database, and delete.

tags.name: blocklist
tags.description: Releases blocked from being grabbed again. Global by design — not scoped per user.

tags.name: book
tags.description: Library book records: listing, retrieval, manual metadata edits, bulk actions, provider rebinding, audiobook enrichment, file download/removal and interactive indexer search.

tags.name: calibre
tags.description: Calibre integration: connection probe, the library-import job, the bulk push-to-Calibre job, and the import-run history with metadata-only rollback. Both jobs follow the same contract — POST returns 202 with an initial progress snapshot, a sibling GET .../status is polled until `running` is false and `finishedAt` is set, and a second POST while one is in flight returns 409. Progress is in-process memory and resets on restart; the durable record is /calibre/runs. The whole subtree is admin-only.

tags.name: customformat
tags.description: Named sets of release-matching conditions (TRaSH-style rules), stored as a JSON blob. Shared deployment config with no owner column — reads and writes are both admin-only so non-admins cannot enumerate which rules are active.

tags.name: delayprofile
tags.description: Per-protocol grab delays letting a better release appear before downloading. Shared deployment config with no owner column — reads and writes are both admin-only so non-admins cannot learn the download policy.

tags.name: downloadclient
tags.description: Download-client configuration, connection tests and completed-path visibility checks. Entirely admin-only — client rows carry cleartext apiKey, username and password.

tags.name: grimmory
tags.description: Grimmory integration: redacted config read, admin config write, connection probe (which performs a real login when credentials exist), and the bulk push-to-BookDrop job. The sync mirrors the Calibre job contract — 202 + snapshot on start, poll .../status, 409 while one is already running — and additionally reports cumulative push totals from the idempotency store.

tags.name: hardcover
tags.description: Hardcover metadata-provider connectivity checks. Admin only.

tags.name: history
tags.description: The event log of grabs, imports, failures and renames. List, delete, or promote an event's release into the blocklist.

tags.name: images
tags.description: Local caching image proxy for external cover art, so the browser never contacts Goodreads / OpenLibrary / Hardcover directly.

tags.name: importlist
tags.description: Import lists: provider-backed shelves (currently Hardcover) that sync books into the catalogue, plus the manual sync trigger and its progress poll. Admin-only — these are shared deployment config and carry provider credentials.

tags.name: importlistexclusion
tags.description: Works blocked from being added by import-list and author catalogue syncs. Admin-only.

tags.name: indexer
tags.description: Newznab/torznab indexer configuration and probes. All CRUD is admin-only because indexer rows carry a cleartext API key; only the freeform search route is open to any authenticated user, and it redacts the indexer apikey out of every result URL.

tags.name: library
tags.description: Library scanning — triggering a reconciliation walk of the configured roots and reading the last scan's result.

tags.name: manual-import
tags.description: Admin-only manual import: look up or scan filesystem paths against the catalogue, import them against a book (singly or in batch), reassign a mis-matched file, and match an import-failed download to a book. Every path is confined to a configured library root.

tags.name: metadataprofile
tags.description: Filters deciding which discovered books are added to the catalogue. Per-user resources (owner_user_id, migration 025): the whole group is open to any authenticated user, and cross-user access on the by-id routes is closed by an ownership check that returns 404.

tags.name: migrate
tags.description: Bulk-import endpoints under /api/v1/migrate. The whole subtree is admin-only (auth.RequireAdmin): these imports parse uploaded files server-side and carry indexer API keys and download-client credentials.

tags.name: notification
tags.description: Outbound webhook notification connections for grab / import / upgrade / failure / health events, plus a live test send. Admin-only because the stored custom headers usually carry credentials.

tags.name: opds
tags.description: OPDS 1.2 catalogue served at `/opds` for reading apps (KOReader, Moon+ Reader, Aldiko). Success responses are Atom XML (`application/atom+xml;profile=opds-catalog;charset=utf-8`) or raw book bytes, never JSON; errors are JSON. The subtree has its own middleware (`api.OPDSAuth`) that adds HTTP Basic on top of the usual API-key / session credentials.

tags.name: pending
tags.description: Releases found by an indexer but not yet grabbed — usually held by a delay profile. List, dismiss, or force-grab them.

tags.name: prowlarr
tags.description: Prowlarr instance configuration and indexer sync. Entirely admin-only — instance rows carry a cleartext API key, and the sync route rewrites local indexer rows.

tags.name: qualityprofile
tags.description: File-format preference lists with an upgrade cutoff, assignable to authors. Reads are open to any authenticated user (with a per-user ownership guard on the by-id read); create/update/delete are admin-only. Deleting a profile still in use by an author is refused with 409.

tags.name: queue
tags.description: The download queue: live-enriched download rows, grabbing releases, retrying imports, and removing items. Includes the Radarr/Sonarr-compatible GET /api/queue projection for external tools.

tags.name: recommendations
tags.description: Per-user recommendation feed: list, accept into the wanted list, dismiss, clear dismissals, and manage author exclusions. Every route is scoped to the authenticated user and ownership mismatches return 404 rather than 403 to avoid leaking existence. The refresh endpoint starts an engine run in the background (202) but, unlike the Calibre/Grimmory jobs, exposes no status endpoint and no already-running guard.

tags.name: reorganize
tags.description: Recompute tracked files' paths from the naming template and move them in place.

tags.name: rootfolder
tags.description: Registered library root directories on the server filesystem. Reads are open to any authenticated caller; registering and removing roots is admin-only.

tags.name: search
tags.description: Metadata-provider search for authors and books (the Add flows), plus re-fetching the caller's most recent release-search audit trail.

tags.name: series
tags.description: Series CRUD, book membership, series-wide genre overrides, filling a series from its Hardcover catalogue, and Hardcover linking/diffing.

tags.name: setting
tags.description: The schema-less key/value settings table. Access is split: reads (list and get) are available to every authenticated user and therefore filter out secret keys entirely, while writes and deletes require the admin role. Only `hardcover.api_token` and `calibre.plugin_api_key` may be written through this generic surface; other secrets have dedicated endpoints.

tags.name: static
tags.description: Non-API routes serving the embedded single-page frontend and its generated runtime configuration script. No auth middleware is mounted on them.

tags.name: system
tags.description: Operational endpoints for running the service, including the unauthenticated Prometheus /metrics exposition mounted at the router root.

tags.name: wanted
tags.description: The wanted/missing queue: listing books with status `wanted` and bulk actions over them.

get.summary: Generated JavaScript exposing the deployment URL base
get.description: Returns a one-line script, built once at startup, that assigns the configured URL base to `window.__BINDERY_BASE__` (e.g. `window.__BINDERY_BASE__="/books";`). It is served as a same-origin external script rather than inlined into `index.html` because the strict CSP (`script-src 'self'`) would silently drop an inline script, breaking the SPA under a path prefix. Sent with `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate`. No auth middleware is mounted on this route.

get.summary: List the queue in a Radarr/Sonarr-compatible shape
get.description:
Radarr/Sonarr-style queue projection for external tools such as Harpoon. It runs the same enrichment as `GET /api/v1/queue` (loads every download row, resolves each referenced download client, and fans out live-status polls with a 1s per-client deadline and a concurrency cap of 4) but projects the result into an *arr `{page,pageSize,sortKey,sortDirection,totalRecords,records}` envelope.

Differences from `GET /api/v1/queue`:
- Envelope is `totalRecords` + `records` (an *arr paged-resource shape), not `items`/`partial`/`staleClients`. Slow/failed download clients are NOT reported here — the `partial` and `staleClients` diagnostics are dropped on the floor.
- Each record is a small flat projection (`id`, `bookId`, `title`, `status`, `trackedDownloadStatus`, `size`, `sizeleft`, `downloadClient`, `downloadId`, `protocol`) instead of the full `Download` row plus `percentage`/`timeLeft`/`speed`/`book`.
- Rows in state `imported` are filtered out; `/api/v1/queue` returns every row.
- `bookId` is coerced to `0` when the download has no linked book (`/api/v1/queue` sends `null`).
- `trackedDownloadStatus` is synthesised: `error` when the row has an error message, a live error status, or is `failed`/`importFailed`/`importBlocked`; `warning` when that row's client poll failed or timed out; otherwise `ok`.
- `size`/`sizeleft` prefer the live client numbers, falling back to the stored size and, if only a percentage is known, to a percentage-derived remainder. Terminal/completed states report `sizeleft: 0`.
- `downloadId` is the remote client id (lowercased torrent hash or SABnzbd nzo id), and `downloadClient` is the client's display name.
- Supports `page`/`pageSize`/`sortKey`/`sortDirection` query parameters; `/api/v1/queue` takes none.
- No `nzbUrl` is exposed at all (so no indexer apikey redaction is needed).

Under tenancy enforcement a non-admin user only sees their own downloads. Read-only: no side effects beyond polling the download clients.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number. Non-numeric or non-positive values are ignored and the default is used. Only honoured when `pageSize` is also supplied.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Records per page. Omitted, non-numeric or non-positive means no pagination — the full record set is returned and `page`/`pageSize` are omitted from the response envelope.

parameters.name: sortKey
parameters.description: Field to sort by, matched case-insensitively. An unrecognised key is echoed back in the response but leaves the order untouched. Omitted means no sorting and `sortKey`/`sortDirection` are omitted from the response envelope.

parameters.name: sortDirection
parameters.description: Sort direction. `descending` and `desc` sort descending; anything else (including an unset or unknown value) is normalised to `ascending`.

500.description: Failed to load downloads.

get.summary: Get the stored Audiobookshelf source configuration
get.description: Reads the `abs.*` settings rows (base URL, label, enabled flag, library IDs, path remap) and returns them. The stored API key is write-only: it is never echoed back, only reported as the boolean `apiKeyConfigured`. `featureEnabled` reflects the server-side feature flag the handler was constructed with. No side effects and no call to the Audiobookshelf server.

put.description: Partial update: every field is a pointer, so an omitted field keeps its currently stored value. Side effects: normalizes the base URL via `abs.NormalizeBaseURL` and validates the API key via `abs.NormalizeAPIKey`, defaults an empty label to `Audiobookshelf`, de-duplicates and trims `libraryIds` (the first entry becomes `libraryId`), then persists all rows atomically through `SettingsRepo.SetMany` so a mid-write failure cannot leave a half-applied config. `apiKey` is only written when present and non-empty — sending an empty string leaves the stored key untouched. Saving never contacts the Audiobookshelf server; use `POST /api/v1/abs/test` for live validation.

200.description: Configuration stored; the resulting normalized config is returned.

400.description: Malformed JSON body, an unparseable base URL, or an invalid API key format.

500.description: Settings could not be marshalled or persisted.

get.summary: List Audiobookshelf vs upstream metadata conflicts
get.description: Returns the paginated conflict list recorded when ABS metadata and upstream metadata disagree on a mapped field. Each row is decorated with a human-readable field label, the currently applied value (resolved from `appliedSource`), the local entity's display name (falling back to the ABS item id) and, for authors, whether the placeholder can be relinked upstream. When no conflict store is configured the handler returns an empty page rather than an error. Read-only.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Non-numeric or non-positive values fall back to the default; values above 100 are clamped to 100.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Row offset. Non-numeric or negative values fall back to 0.

500.description: The conflict store or the referenced author/book could not be read.

post.summary: Resolve a metadata conflict by choosing a source
post.description: Picks the winning value for a conflicted field. The conflict is claimed atomically first to close a TOCTOU race where two concurrent calls both read `pending` and write divergent values; if the claim fails the handler re-reads and returns the current (already-resolved) state with 200 instead of erroring. On a successful claim it writes the chosen value onto the local author or book via `ApplyAuthorConflictValue` / `ApplyBookConflictValue`, stamps `lastMetadataRefreshAt`, then persists `appliedSource`, `preferredSource` and `resolutionStatus = "resolved"`. A failure while applying the value unclaims the conflict and returns 500. Conflicts on an entity type other than `author` or `book` are marked resolved without touching any entity.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Conflict id (int64).

400.description: Non-numeric id, malformed body, or a `source` other than `abs` / `upstream`.

404.description: No conflict store configured, or conflict not found.

500.description: The claim, the entity update or the conflict write failed.

post.summary: Start an Audiobookshelf import run
post.description: Builds an `abs.ImportConfig` from the stored settings (source id, base URL, API key, library IDs, path remap, label, enabled flag), overriding only `dryRun` from the body, validates it (the source must be enabled and have a base URL, API key and at least one library ID), then launches the importer asynchronously on a context detached from the request. Each selected library is scanned sequentially and gets its own run row, checkpoint, summary, rollback scope and provenance; a failing library aborts the remaining ones while preserving completed runs. Returns immediately with the current progress snapshot — poll `GET /api/v1/abs/import/status` for the outcome.

requestBody.description: Optional dry-run toggle. An empty body starts a normal (non-dry-run) import.

202.description: Import accepted and running; initial progress snapshot.

400.description: Malformed body, invalid config (source disabled, empty base URL/API key, no library IDs), or the importer refused to start.

409.description: An import is already running (`abs.ErrAlreadyRunning`).

get.description: Returns the 10 most recent persisted import runs (the limit is hard-coded in the handler; there are no query parameters). Each stored row is hydrated via `abs.HydrateRun`, which decodes the run's stored source-config, checkpoint and summary JSON into structured objects.

200.description: Up to 10 recent runs, newest first (possibly empty).

500.description: The run store could not be read.

post.summary: Roll back an import run
post.description: Executes the rollback plan for the given run: deletes entities the run created and unlinks the provenance rows it wrote, skipping anything that has since been modified or is referenced elsewhere. Destructive and not itself undoable — call the preview endpoint first. Returns the applied actions and statistics.

parameters.name: runID
parameters.description: Import run id. Must parse as a positive int64.

400.description: Missing/non-numeric/non-positive run id, unknown run, or the rollback failed.

post.summary: Preview the rollback of an import run
post.description: Plans — but does not execute — the rollback of the given run: enumerates the entities the run created or linked and returns the actions that would be taken plus the resulting statistics. No entity is deleted and no provenance is unlinked. Use `POST /api/v1/abs/import/runs/{runID}/rollback` to apply it.

parameters.name: runID
parameters.description: Import run id. Must parse as a positive int64.

400.description: Missing/non-numeric/non-positive run id, unknown run, or the planner rejected the request.

get.description: Returns the importer's in-memory progress snapshot: whether a run is active, the active run id, processed count, latest message/error, resume state, the enumeration checkpoint, aggregate stats and per-item results. Read-only; safe to poll. The request itself is ignored by the handler.

post.summary: List the Audiobookshelf book libraries visible to the API key
post.description: Live probe that calls the Audiobookshelf libraries endpoint using the saved base URL plus either the API key in the body or the stored key, then filters the result to `mediaType == "book"` — podcast and other non-book libraries are omitted because the importer refuses them. POST rather than GET because it accepts an API-key override in the body. Read-only: the selection is not persisted, save it with `PUT /api/v1/abs/config`. Error mapping matches `POST /api/v1/abs/test`.

requestBody.description: Optional API-key override. An empty body is accepted and falls back to the stored key.

200.description: Book libraries visible to the key (possibly empty).

400.description: Malformed body, no saved base URL, missing/invalid API key, or ABS returned 404.

502.description: Audiobookshelf rejected the API key or was unreachable.

get.description: Returns the paginated `pending` review queue — the ambiguously matched authors and books the importer parked instead of guessing (unmatched items are imported directly and are never queued). For each item the handler decodes the stored payload and re-evaluates file visibility against the current ABS config, populating `fileMappingFound` / `fileMappingMessage`; items whose payload JSON fails to decode are returned without that decoration. Read-only.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Non-numeric or non-positive values fall back to the default; values above 100 are clamped to 100.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Row offset. Non-numeric or negative values fall back to 0.

500.description: The review store could not be read.

post.summary: Dismiss every review item queued by an import run
post.description: Bulk-dismisses the whole review backlog produced by one import run. When a run store is wired the run is looked up first and an unknown run yields 404; otherwise the dismissal proceeds directly. Returns how many rows were dismissed. Takes no request body.

parameters.name: runID
parameters.description: Import run id. Must parse as a positive int64.

400.description: Missing, non-numeric or non-positive run id.

404.description: Import run not found.

500.description: The run lookup or the bulk dismissal failed.

post.summary: Approve a review item and import it
post.description: Applies the item's stored author/book resolutions and edited title to its saved payload, validates an import config built from the item's own source and library id plus the stored ABS settings, marks the item `approved` **before** importing (so a crash leaves an approved-but-not-imported item rather than a silent duplicate), then runs `ImportReview` to create/link the author, book, series, edition and provenance rows. If the import fails the status is reverted to `pending` and 400 is returned. Takes no request body. Rejects an item that has already left the `pending` state with 409, which is what stops a double-click from importing the book twice.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Review item id. Must parse as a positive int64.

200.description: Item imported; the refreshed review row is returned.

400.description: Missing/invalid id, a lookup failure, an undecodable stored payload, an invalid import config, or the import itself failed.

404.description: Review item not found.

409.description: The review item is no longer pending.

500.description: The status update or the re-read of the item failed.

post.summary: Dismiss a review item
post.description: Sets the item's status to `dismissed` so it drops out of the pending queue. Nothing is imported and the underlying ABS item is untouched. Takes no request body. Returns the refreshed review row.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Review item id. Must parse as a positive int64.

400.description: Missing or invalid review item id.

404.description: Review item not found.

500.description: The status update or the re-read of the item failed.

post.summary: Pin the author match for a review item's primary author
post.description: Records the chosen upstream author for the item's primary author. The write is deliberately **bulk**: `ResolveAuthorForPrimary` updates every pending review item sharing the same source id, library id and primary author, and returns how many rows changed — the path `{id}` only selects the item whose primary author is being resolved. Does not import anything; approve the items separately. `applyTo`, when non-empty, must be `same_author`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Review item id. Must parse as a positive int64.

400.description: Missing/invalid id, malformed body, an `applyTo` other than `same_author`, or the store rejected the update.

404.description: Review item not found.

post.summary: Pin the book match for a review item
post.description: Stores the chosen upstream book id, its title and an optional operator-edited title on this single review item. The edited title replaces the payload title when the item is later approved. Does not import anything — call approve afterwards. Returns the refreshed review row.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Review item id. Must parse as a positive int64.

400.description: Missing/invalid id, malformed body, or the store rejected the update.

404.description: Review item not found.

500.description: The re-read of the item failed.

post.summary: Probe the configured Audiobookshelf server
post.description: Live connection test. Calls the Audiobookshelf `authorize` endpoint using the saved base URL and either the API key supplied in the body or, when absent, the stored key. The base URL must already be saved — the handler never takes it from the request body. On an ABS 401/403 it reports `ABS rejected the API key` as 502; on an ABS 404 it reports `library not found or not accessible` as 400; other transport failures return 502, with a LAN/VPN-killswitch hint substituted for a bare client timeout against a LAN host. Read-only: nothing is persisted.

requestBody.description: Optional API-key override. An empty body is accepted and falls back to the stored key.

400.description: Malformed body, no saved base URL, missing/invalid API key, or ABS returned 404.

502.description: Audiobookshelf rejected the API key or was unreachable.

post.summary: Roll the instance API key and return the new value
post.description:
Generates a fresh 32-byte random hex key, persists it to the `auth.api_key` setting, logs `api key regenerated`, and returns the new key in the response body — this is the only time it is handed back other than via `GET /api/v1/auth/config` for an admin. Every client using the previous key (as `X-Api-Key` or `?apikey=`) stops authenticating immediately.

Admin-only: mounted inside the `auth.RequireAdmin` group. Mutating, so a browser caller also needs `X-Requested-With: bindery-ui` and a valid `X-CSRF-Token`; API-key-authenticated callers are exempt from both.

403.description: Admin role required, or the request failed the CSRF / `X-Requested-With` guards.

500.description: Random generation or the settings write failed.

get.description:
Returns the effective auth mode, the caller's username, and — **only when the request context carries the `admin` role** — the current API key. Non-admin callers get an empty `apiKey`. When no user id is on the context (auth mode `disabled` or `local-only` bypass) the handler falls back to the single existing user's username.

Requires authentication: this path is not in `auth.AllowUnauthPath`, so the standard middleware applies — a valid `bindery_session` cookie, an `X-Api-Key` header, a `?apikey=` query parameter (honoured on safe methods only), or a mode-based bypass (`disabled`, or `local-only` from a trusted local peer).

200.description: Auth configuration. `apiKey` is populated for admin callers only.

401.description: Not authenticated (emitted by the auth middleware).

get.summary: Issue a double-submit CSRF token bound to the caller's session
get.description:
Derives an HMAC CSRF token from the current session signing secret and the raw value of the caller's `bindery_session` cookie. The token is returned as JSON **and** written as a readable (non-`HttpOnly`) `bindery_csrf` cookie with `Path=/`, `SameSite=Lax`, so browser JS can read it and replay it as the `X-CSRF-Token` header on mutating requests. The `Secure` attribute follows `BINDERY_COOKIE_SECURE` (`always` / `never` / `auto` — `auto` detects `r.TLS` or `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`).

A caller with no session cookie gets `200` with an empty `csrfToken` — there is nothing to bind to, and the CSRF middleware only enforces the token when a session cookie is present.

Reachable unauthenticated: listed in `auth.AllowUnauthPath`.

200.description: CSRF token (empty string when the caller has no session cookie).

Set-Cookie.description: `bindery_csrf=<token>; Path=/; SameSite=Lax` — deliberately not HttpOnly. Omitted when the caller has no session cookie.

post.summary: Log in with a local username and password
post.description:
Rate-limited per client IP by `auth.LoginLimiter`; a rejected attempt is recorded and a successful one resets the counter. The password is always verified against a dummy Argon2 hash when the username does not exist so a missing user and a wrong password take the same time (no username enumeration by timing).

On success the handler mints a signed session cookie `bindery_session` (`HttpOnly`, `Path=/`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure` per `BINDERY_COOKIE_SECURE`) carrying the user id, the user's current `session_epoch`, and an expiry — 12 hours normally, 30 days when `rememberMe` is true (in which case the cookie also gets an `Expires` attribute).

Returns `403` when local password auth is disabled (`BINDERY_LOCAL_AUTH_ENABLED=false`).

Reachable unauthenticated: listed in `auth.AllowUnauthPath`, so it needs neither `X-Requested-With: bindery-ui` nor `X-CSRF-Token`.

400.description: Body is not valid JSON.

401.description: Invalid credentials (unknown username or wrong password — indistinguishable by design).

403.description: Local password login is disabled on this instance.

429.description: Too many failed attempts from this client IP.

500.description: User lookup, password hashing, or session signing failed.

post.summary: Clear the session cookie
post.description:
Expires the `bindery_session` cookie by re-setting it empty with `MaxAge=-1` (`Path=/`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`). The request body is ignored and no server-side state is touched — sessions are stateless signed cookies, so this only affects the calling browser. Always succeeds.

Reachable unauthenticated: listed in `auth.AllowUnauthPath`.

put.description:
Persists the `auth.mode` setting and logs `auth mode changed`. The submitted value is coerced by `auth.ParseMode`: anything outside the known set falls back to `enabled` (fail-safe), and the coerced value is what the response echoes.

The mode governs the middleware: `enabled` — everyone authenticates; `local-only` — RFC1918/loopback peers bypass auth and are treated as admin; `disabled` — no auth check at all; `proxy` — identity is trusted from the configured upstream header when the peer is inside a trusted-proxy CIDR. Note that `disabled` and `local-only` change who counts as admin for every other endpoint, so this route can lock or unlock the whole instance.

Admin-only: mounted inside the `auth.RequireAdmin` group. Mutating, so browser callers need `X-Requested-With: bindery-ui` and a valid `X-CSRF-Token`.

200.description: The mode actually persisted, after coercion.

400.description: Body is not valid JSON.

403.description: Admin role required, or the request failed the CSRF / `X-Requested-With` guards.

500.description: The settings write failed.

get.summary: List configured OIDC providers with runtime status
get.description:
Reads the `auth.oidc.providers` setting and returns the API-safe view of each provider (`client_secret` is never included) paired with its live status from the in-memory manager: `ok` when discovery succeeded, `failed` (with `last_error`) when it did not. A provider present in the DB but missing from the manager is unusable for login until discovery recovers. Returns `[]` when nothing is configured.

Reachable unauthenticated on **GET only** — `auth.AllowUnauthPath` special-cases this path so the login page can render provider buttons before the user has a session. `PUT` on the same path is admin-gated.

500.description: The stored provider JSON could not be parsed.

put.description:
Takes the full provider array and replaces the `auth.oidc.providers` setting with it. Secrets are merged rather than clobbered: when an incoming provider omits `client_secret` (empty string), the secret stored under the same `id` is preserved; if no such provider exists yet the request is rejected with `400` naming the offending id. After persisting, the manager is reloaded **asynchronously** in a goroutine anchored to the process lifetime context, so the response returns without waiting on IdP discovery — a provider may briefly report `failed` on the next `GET` while discovery is in flight.

Admin-only: mounted inside the `auth.RequireAdmin` group; `auth.AllowUnauthPath` deliberately allows only the GET on this path. Mutating, so browser callers need `X-Requested-With: bindery-ui` and a valid `X-CSRF-Token`.

400.description: Body is not valid JSON, or a new provider was submitted without `client_secret`.

403.description: Admin role required, or the request failed the CSRF / `X-Requested-With` guards.

500.description: Marshalling the merged config or the settings write failed.

get.summary: Preview the public base URL used for OIDC callback URLs
get.description:
Resolves the public-facing base URL for the current request — `BINDERY_OIDC_REDIRECT_BASE_URL` when set, otherwise derived from forwarded headers / `Host` — and returns it alongside the callback path template `/api/v1/auth/oidc/{id}/callback`. The Settings UI concatenates the two to show an exact copy-pasteable redirect URI. `configured: false` means the base was derived from request headers and may differ from what the IdP actually receives, so the UI should warn.

Requires authentication: not listed in `auth.AllowUnauthPath`, so a session cookie, `X-Api-Key` / `?apikey=`, or a mode-based bypass is needed.

200.description: Resolved redirect base and callback path template.

post.summary: Probe an issuer's OIDC discovery document
post.description:
Server-side outbound probe of `<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration`, exposed as the Settings UI's "Test" button. Returns the parsed metadata plus `issuer_mismatch`, which is true when the IdP's own `issuer` differs from the value submitted — the silent killer behind Authentik per-provider mode and Keycloak realm paths.

Contract quirk: an unreachable IdP, a TLS/DNS error, a non-2xx, a parse failure, or an SSRF refusal all come back as **HTTP 200** with `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}` so the UI can render the message inline; `400` is reserved for malformed input (bad JSON, empty issuer).

SSRF guard: the issuer URL and every redirect hop are validated against `httpsec.PolicyLAN`, which blocks loopback, link-local, and cloud-metadata destinations while still allowing RFC1918 on-prem IdPs. Setting `BINDERY_ALLOW_LAN_OIDC=1|true` disables the guard entirely and fetches whatever URL is submitted.

Requires authentication (not in `auth.AllowUnauthPath`); being mutating it also needs `X-Requested-With: bindery-ui` and a valid `X-CSRF-Token` from a browser caller. It is not inside the `RequireAdmin` group, so any authenticated user can trigger the outbound fetch.

200.description: Probe finished. Check `ok` — a failed probe is still a 200.

400.description: Body is not valid JSON, or `issuer` is empty.

get.summary: Complete the OIDC code exchange and issue a Bindery session
get.description:
The IdP redirect target. Steps, in order: validate the provider id; read and decode the `bindery_oidc_flow` cookie and immediately expire it; compare the `state` query parameter against the sealed value; surface any IdP `error`; require a `code`; exchange the code for an ID token using the pinned redirect base, the sealed nonce, and the PKCE verifier.

After the token validates:

1. **AllowedGroups policy** — when the provider configures `allowed_groups`, the user's groups (read from the operator-configured claim, `BINDERY_OIDC_GROUP_CLAIM`, default `groups`) must intersect it. Fail-closed: a missing or misnamed claim rejects every login with `403`.
2. **Identity resolution** — look up by `(issuer, sub)`; optionally link to an existing account by email, but only when the IdP asserts `email_verified: true` (an unverified email would be an account-takeover vector, so it is skipped and logged).
3. **Auto-provision or deny** — an unknown subject creates a user when auto-provisioning is on, otherwise `403`. The provisioning role is `BINDERY_OIDC_DEFAULT_ROLE`, upgraded to `admin` only by the one-shot promote-first-user fallback (local auth disabled, zero admins in the DB, guard setting unclaimed — raced atomically via `SetIfAbsent`).
4. **Group-claim role sync** — when `BINDERY_OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP` is set, the IdP is authoritative on every login: present promotes to `admin`, absent demotes to `user`. This deliberately overrides any role set through `PUT /api/v1/auth/users/{id}/role`.

On success it issues a 30-day `bindery_session` cookie and 302-redirects to `/`.

Reachable unauthenticated: `auth.AllowUnauthPath` allows any `/api/v1/auth/oidc/**/callback` path.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Configured provider id. Validated against `^[a-z0-9_-]{1,32}$`.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Opaque state echoed by the IdP; must equal the value sealed in the `bindery_oidc_flow` cookie.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Authorization code to exchange. Required on the success path — absent (and no `error` present) yields 400 `missing code`.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: OAuth 2.0 error code returned by the IdP instead of a `code`. Its presence short-circuits to 401.

parameters.name: error_description
parameters.description: Human-readable IdP error detail; logged (CRLF-sanitised), never echoed to the caller.

302.description: Login succeeded; session cookie issued and the browser is sent to the UI root.

Set-Cookie.description: `bindery_session=<signed value>; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax` (30 days), plus the expiry of `bindery_oidc_flow`.

400.description: Invalid provider id, missing or undecodable flow cookie, state mismatch, or missing `code`.

401.description: The IdP returned an error, or the token exchange / ID-token validation failed.

403.description: Rejected by the provider's `allowed_groups` policy, or the subject is unknown and auto-provisioning is disabled.

500.description: User lookup, email lookup, subject linking, provisioning, or group-claim role sync failed.

get.summary: Start the OIDC Authorization Code + PKCE flow
get.description:
Generates a fresh `state`, `nonce`, and PKCE code verifier, builds the provider's authorize URL against the resolved redirect base, and **302-redirects the browser to the IdP**. The three values plus the resolved redirect base are sealed into a short-lived `bindery_oidc_flow` cookie (`Path=/api/v1/auth/oidc`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Max-Age=600`, `Secure` per `BINDERY_COOKIE_SECURE`) so the callback can verify them with no server-side session store. The redirect base is round-tripped because the IdP requires the token-exchange `redirect_uri` to match the authorize one.

Reachable unauthenticated: `auth.AllowUnauthPath` allows any `/api/v1/auth/oidc/**/login` path — the IdP round-trip necessarily happens before the user holds a Bindery session.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Configured provider id. Validated against `^[a-z0-9_-]{1,32}$`.

302.description: Redirect to the IdP authorization endpoint; flow-state cookie set.

Location.description: The IdP authorize URL, including `state`, `nonce`, and the PKCE challenge.

400.description: Provider id fails the id pattern, or the provider is unknown / its discovery has not loaded.

500.description: Generating state / nonce / verifier or encoding the flow cookie failed.

post.summary: Change the authenticated user's password
post.description:
Verifies `currentPassword` against the stored Argon2 hash, then writes the new hash via `UpdatePassword`, which atomically bumps the user's `session_epoch`. Because every signed session cookie carries the epoch it was minted under, that bump invalidates **all** outstanding cookies for the user — so the handler immediately re-issues a fresh 30-day `bindery_session` cookie for the caller (other browsers and any stolen cookie are evicted). The re-issue is skipped on the single-user fallback path below, which has no cookie to preserve.

Fallback: under auth mode `disabled` or `local-only` there may be no user id on the context. In that case the handler proceeds only when exactly one user exists and acts on that user; otherwise it returns `401`.

Requires authentication and, for a browser caller, the CSRF pair: `X-Requested-With: bindery-ui` plus an `X-CSRF-Token` matching the `bindery_csrf` cookie. Requests authenticated by API key are exempt from both guards.

200.description: Password changed; a fresh session cookie is issued when the caller was logged in.

Set-Cookie.description: `bindery_session=<signed value>; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax` — re-minted with the post-bump epoch.

400.description: Invalid JSON body, or the new password is shorter than 8 characters.

401.description: Not logged in, user not found, or `currentPassword` is incorrect.

403.description: Rejected by the CSRF guards — missing `X-Requested-With: bindery-ui`, or an absent/mismatched `X-CSRF-Token` while a session cookie is present.

500.description: Hashing or the password update failed.

post.summary: Rotate the session cookie signing secret
post.description:
Mints a new base64 secret, moves the current one into `auth.session_secret_previous`, and writes both keys atomically via `SettingsRepo.SetMany` so no verifier ever observes a half-applied rotation. Logs `session signing secret rotated`.

Effect on live sessions: new cookies and CSRF tokens are signed with the new secret, while existing `bindery_session` cookies keep verifying because verification is handed the ordered set `{current, previous}`. The grace window closes at the *next* rotation, which overwrites the previous slot — twice-rotated-out cookies stop verifying and those users must log in again.

Admin-only: mounted inside the `auth.RequireAdmin` group. Mutating, so browser callers need `X-Requested-With: bindery-ui` and a valid `X-CSRF-Token`.

403.description: Admin role required, or the request failed the CSRF / `X-Requested-With` guards.

500.description: Random generation or the atomic settings write failed.

post.summary: Create the first admin user (first-run only)
post.description:
Only permitted while the users table is empty; returns `409` once any user exists. Creates the account with an Argon2 password hash, promotes it to the `admin` role (`PromoteFirstUser`), and immediately logs the caller in by issuing a 30-day `bindery_session` cookie. Logs `first-run setup complete`.

Validation: username must be non-empty after trimming and the password must be at least 8 characters.

Reachable unauthenticated: listed in `auth.AllowUnauthPath`.

200.description: Admin created and logged in; session cookie issued.

400.description: Invalid JSON body, empty username, or password shorter than 8 characters.

409.description: Setup already complete — at least one user exists.

500.description: Counting users, hashing, user creation, promotion, or session signing failed.

get.summary: Report authentication state and whether first-run setup is required
get.description:
Public probe the frontend hits on page load. Counts the rows in the users table and reports `setupRequired: true` when it is zero. Identity is resolved by the auth middleware before the handler runs: a valid `bindery_session` cookie (or, in `proxy` mode, a trusted upstream identity header) attaches the user id to the request context, and the handler then echoes the username and role. When no user id is present but the request has admin semantics (auth mode `disabled`, or mode `local-only` from an RFC1918/loopback peer), the response reports `authenticated: true` with `role: "admin"` so role-gated UI renders without a login screen.

Reachable unauthenticated: listed in `auth.AllowUnauthPath`, so the middleware always lets it through, and it is exempt from the `X-Requested-With: bindery-ui` and `X-CSRF-Token` guards.

500.description: Counting users failed.

get.description:
Returns every user with id, username, role, optional email and display name, and creation timestamp. Password hashes and OIDC subject identifiers are never included. Returns `[]` when the table is empty.

Admin-only: mounted inside the `auth.RequireAdmin` group.

500.description: Listing users failed.

post.summary: Create a local user
post.description:
Hashes the supplied password with Argon2 and inserts the user. When `role` is exactly `"admin"` the new row is promoted straight after creation; any other value (including omitted) leaves the repository default `user`.

Rejected with `403` when local password accounts are disabled (`BINDERY_LOCAL_AUTH_ENABLED=false`). A duplicate username surfaces as `500` from the repository's insert error rather than a `409`.

Admin-only: mounted inside the `auth.RequireAdmin` group. Mutating, so browser callers need `X-Requested-With: bindery-ui` and a valid `X-CSRF-Token`.

201.description: User created.

400.description: Invalid JSON body, missing username or password, or a password shorter than 8 characters.

403.description: Admin role required, local accounts are disabled, or the request failed the CSRF / `X-Requested-With` guards.

500.description: Hashing, insertion (including a duplicate username), or the role promotion failed.

delete.description:
Removes the user inside a transaction that first re-reads their role and refuses to delete the last remaining admin — that guard surfaces as `400` with the repository's message (`cannot delete the last admin user`), as does any other repository error including an unknown id.

Admin-only: mounted inside the `auth.RequireAdmin` group. Mutating, so browser callers need `X-Requested-With: bindery-ui` and a valid `X-CSRF-Token`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: User id (parsed with `strconv.ParseInt`).

400.description: Id is not an integer, the user does not exist, or the delete would remove the last admin.

403.description: Admin role required, or the request failed the CSRF / `X-Requested-With` guards.

put.summary: Set a new password for a user
put.description:
Admin password reset: hashes the supplied password with Argon2 and calls `UpdatePassword`, which atomically bumps the target user's `session_epoch`. Every outstanding `bindery_session` cookie for that user therefore stops verifying and they are logged out everywhere. The current password is **not** required. No new cookie is minted here — the target user must log in again.

Admin-only: mounted inside the `auth.RequireAdmin` group. Mutating, so browser callers need `X-Requested-With: bindery-ui` and a valid `X-CSRF-Token`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: User id (parsed with `strconv.ParseInt`).

200.description: Password reset; the target user's existing sessions are invalidated.

400.description: Id is not an integer, body is not valid JSON, or the password is shorter than 8 characters.

403.description: Admin role required, or the request failed the CSRF / `X-Requested-With` guards.

500.description: Hashing or the password update failed.

put.description:
Sets the role to `admin` or `user`. The repository validates the value and, in a transaction, refuses to demote the last remaining admin; both conditions come back as `400` carrying the repository message (`invalid role ...` / `cannot demote the last admin user`).

Caveat: for OIDC users this is not the final word — when `BINDERY_OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP` is configured, the next OIDC login re-syncs the role from the IdP group claim and overwrites whatever is set here.

Admin-only: mounted inside the `auth.RequireAdmin` group. Mutating, so browser callers need `X-Requested-With: bindery-ui` and a valid `X-CSRF-Token`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: User id (parsed with `strconv.ParseInt`).

400.description: Id is not an integer, body is not valid JSON, role is not `admin`/`user`, or the change would demote the last admin.

403.description: Admin role required, or the request failed the CSRF / `X-Requested-With` guards.

get.description: Returns a paginated page of authors wrapped in `{items,total,limit,offset}`. The list is tenancy-scoped: admins and API-key callers see the whole shared library, non-admin users see their own plus unowned rows. Each returned author has its description run through the HTML/markup cleaner and its imageUrl rewritten to the local image proxy. Books, aliases, statistics and lastSync are NOT attached by the list endpoint — fetch a single author for those.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Non-numeric or non-positive values fall back to the default; values above the maximum are clamped to it.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Row offset. Negative or non-numeric values fall back to 0.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the author name. Trimmed; empty disables the filter.

parameters.name: monitored
parameters.description: Restrict to monitored (`true`) or unmonitored (`false`) authors. Any other value is ignored and no monitored filter is applied.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Whitelisted sort key. Unknown values fall back to `az` (sort_name ascending).

500.description: Database error listing authors.

post.summary: Add an author to the library
post.description: Adds an author by upstream (metadata provider) id. Side effects: fetches the author's profile from the metadata aggregator (external API call); checks for an existing row with the same or an aliased foreign id and for a canonical name/alias match; when the local match is a relinkable placeholder (Calibre/Audiobookshelf-sourced or id-less) it is relinked in place to the upstream identity, recording alias rows for the previous name and id; otherwise it inserts a new author row owned by the calling user, records alias rows for the requested name and any provider alternate names, marks the `first author added` telemetry milestone, and spawns an asynchronous catalogue sync that creates the author's books (and, when `searchOnAdd` is set, queues indexer searches for them).

200.description: An existing relinkable local author was adopted for the requested upstream identity and its catalogue sync was queued.

201.description: Author created; catalogue sync queued asynchronously.

400.description: Malformed JSON, missing `foreignAuthorId`/`authorName`, invalid `monitorMode`, or non-positive `monitorLatestCount`.

409.description: The author already exists, the name resolves ambiguously, or it resolves to an existing author that must be merged manually. The body carries `canonicalAuthorId`/`canonicalAuthor` when a specific conflicting row was identified.

502.description: The metadata provider could not be reached or returned no usable author.

500.description: Database error while looking up or inserting the author.

post.summary: Add a single book (creating its author if needed)
post.description: Adds one work by provider book id. When `foreignAuthorId` is omitted the handler resolves the owning author from the book id (external provider calls), falling back to name-based resolution against the local library and then the canonical provider. It then finds or creates the author (created unmonitored, on the default metadata profile, collapsing a synthetic DNB-only row onto the canonical identity when one exists), triggers a catalogue sync for the requested work, and polls the database for up to 15 seconds until the book row exists. The book is then marked monitored, its media type is overridden when requested (re-evaluating status), and — with `searchOnAdd` — an indexer search-and-grab is dispatched in the background. If the poll never sees the book, a speculatively created author with no books is rolled back.

201.description: The book row now exists, is monitored, and is returned.

400.description: Malformed JSON, missing `foreignBookId`, or a `mediaType` outside ebook/audiobook/both.

404.description: The book did not appear within the 15-second sync poll window.

409.description: A concurrent request already inserted the author and the row could not be re-read.

422.description: No author could be resolved for the requested book — the author must be added manually first.

502.description: The metadata provider failed while resolving the book's author.

504.description: The client cancelled the request while the handler was polling for the book.

500.description: The author could not be resolved or the book update failed.

post.summary: Apply a bulk action to several authors
post.description: Applies one action to every id in the request and returns a per-id result map with HTTP 200 even when individual ids fail (stale ids are reported inline rather than aborting the batch). Actions: `monitor`/`unmonitor` toggle the monitored flag; `delete` removes the author row (cascading its books); `search` collects every wanted+monitored book of each author and dispatches indexer searches after the response under a bounded, rate-paced pool; `refresh` re-reads each author's metadata from the provider under the same bounded pool (metadata only, never auto-grabs); `set_media_type` rewrites the media type of every book belonging to each author; `set_monitor_mode` sets the author monitor mode (and optionally `monitorNewItems`, `monitorLatestCount`) and can re-apply it to existing books. Every id is ownership-checked; a non-owned id is reported as `author not found` in its result entry.

200.description: Per-id results. Individual entries may carry an error while the request as a whole succeeded.

400.description: Malformed JSON, empty `ids`, unknown `action`, `refresh` not wired on this server, invalid `mediaType` for set_media_type, or an invalid/`series` `monitorMode`, `monitorLatestCount` or `monitorNewItems` for set_monitor_mode.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Local author id.

get.summary: Get one author with joined detail
get.description: Returns the author with its books (owner-scoped, matching `GET /book?authorId=`), its alias rows, the pinned monitored-series id set when the author is in `series` monitor mode, and the in-process summary of the most recent catalogue sync (absent until this process has synced the author). The description is cleaned and the image URL is rewritten to the local proxy. A cross-user id returns 404 rather than 403 so non-owners cannot probe for existence.

400.description: `id` is not an integer.

404.description: No such author, or it belongs to another user.

500.description: Database error loading the author.

put.summary: Update an author's monitoring and profile settings
put.description: Partial update: only the fields present in the body are applied. Persists the author row, then optionally replaces the per-author monitored-series pin set (every id is validated to belong to one of this author's own series) and, when `applyMonitorModeToExisting` is set, rewrites the monitored flag of every existing book according to the resulting monitor mode. Metadata fields (name, description, image) are not editable here.

400.description: Non-integer `id`, malformed JSON, invalid `monitorMode`/`monitorNewItems`, non-positive `monitorLatestCount`, or a `monitoredSeriesIds` entry that does not belong to this author.

404.description: No such author, or it belongs to another user.

500.description: Database error updating the author, its series pins, or its books.

delete.description: Deletes the author row; the foreign-key cascade removes its books and book_files rows. With `deleteFiles=true` every tracked file path (including excluded books and audiobook folders) is collected before the delete and swept from disk afterwards — each path is checked for containment inside a configured library root and skipped with a warning if it falls outside, and paths still owned by a surviving book of another author are left alone. Per-file errors are logged, not returned. The in-process catalogue-sync accounting for the id is discarded so a re-added author cannot inherit it.

parameters.name: deleteFiles
parameters.description: Set to the literal string `true` to also remove the author's book files from disk. Any other value leaves files in place.

400.description: `id` is not an integer.

404.description: No such author, or it belongs to another user.

500.description: Database error deleting the author.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Canonical (target) author id.

get.description: Returns every alternate-name row pointing at this canonical author. Aliases are created by the add/relink flows (previous names, requested spellings, provider alternate names) and by merges. Returns an empty array when the author has none.

400.description: `id` is not an integer.

404.description: No such author, or it belongs to another user.

500.description: Database error loading the author or its aliases.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Canonical author id the alias belongs to.

parameters.name: aliasID
parameters.description: Alias row id.

delete.summary: Delete one alias from an author
delete.description: Removes a single alias row, scoped to the author in the path — an alias belonging to a different author is reported as not found. Deleting an alias only drops the alternate-name mapping used for release-name matching and duplicate collapsing; it does not touch books.

400.description: `id` or `aliasID` is not an integer.

404.description: No such author (or it belongs to another user), or no such alias on that author.

500.description: Database error deleting the alias.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Local author id.

put.summary: Set and lock a genre list on every book of an author
put.description: Writes the given genre list onto every book belonging to the author and locks the `genres` field on each so metadata refresh and enrichment can never overwrite it. Entries are trimmed and empties dropped, preserving order; an empty list is valid and means "no genres, and stop refilling them". The first persistence failure aborts, but the operation is idempotent and the response's `updated` count reports how far it got.

400.description: `id` is not an integer, or the body is malformed JSON.

404.description: No such author, or it belongs to another user.

500.description: Database error listing or updating the author's books.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Target (canonical) author id — the author the source is merged INTO.

post.summary: Merge one author into another
post.description: Collapses the source author into the target author in a single transaction: every book pointing at the source is reparented to the target, the source's aliases and provider identifiers are repointed, the source's name and foreign id become alias rows on the target, and the source row is deleted. With `overwriteDefaults` (default true) the target inherits the source's monitored flag, profile ids and root folder. Both ids are ownership-checked up front.

200.description: Merge counts. Note this body uses Go field names (capitalised), not camelCase — the struct carries no JSON tags.

400.description: Non-integer `id`, malformed JSON, missing `sourceId`, or source equal to target.

404.description: Either the source or the target author does not exist or belongs to another user. The message names the offending id.

500.description: The merge transaction failed.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Local author id.

post.summary: Refresh an author's metadata and catalogue
post.description: Queues an asynchronous catalogue sync for the author and returns immediately. The sync re-reads the author's profile and works from the metadata provider and may create rows for newly discovered works — subject to the author's monitoring policy (`monitored` and `monitorNewItems`) — using the global default media type. It never queues indexer grabs. Results of the run are exposed as `lastSync` on the author detail endpoint.

202.description: Refresh accepted and running in the background.

400.description: `id` is not an integer.

404.description: No such author, or it belongs to another user.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Local author id.

post.summary: Relink a local author to upstream metadata
post.description: Repoints a local author (typically one created from a Calibre/Audiobookshelf import with no real provider identity) at an upstream metadata record. With an explicit `foreignAuthorId` that record is fetched directly; otherwise the aggregator is searched by the author's name and a confident, unambiguous match is required. On success the upstream foreign id, name, sort name, description, image, disambiguation, ratings and provider are merged into the local row, the previous foreign id is preserved as an author identifier, alias rows are recorded for the old and requested names, and `lastMetadataRefreshAt` is stamped. The body may be empty (relink by the author's current name). Sending a `foreignAuthorId` also bypasses the guard that rejects authors already linked upstream.

400.description: Non-integer `id`, or a malformed (non-empty) JSON body.

404.description: No such author, or it belongs to another user.

409.description: The author is already linked upstream, no confident match was found, the name resolves ambiguously, or the upstream identity already exists locally. Carries `canonicalAuthorId`/`canonicalAuthor` when a specific conflicting row was identified.

424.description: No metadata aggregator is configured on this server.

502.description: The metadata provider call failed.

500.description: Database error while resolving conflicts or persisting the relink.

parameters.name: id

post.summary: Snapshot the live database into the backups directory
post.description:
`BackupHandler.Create` (internal/api/backup.go). Side effects: creates `<dataDir>/backups` (mode 0700) if absent, runs SQLite `VACUUM INTO` against the live database to produce a WAL-consistent, self-contained snapshot, chmods it to 0600 (so bcrypt hashes / session secrets / the API key are not left world-readable), and atomically renames it into place as `bindery_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>[_<label>].db`. A stale `.tmp` from a previous failed run in the same UTC second is removed first. The operation is O(database size) — seconds on a multi-GB library — and its duration is logged and returned.

The request body is OPTIONAL: it is read through a 4 KiB limit reader and a missing, empty or malformed body is simply ignored, leaving the backup with a plain timestamp name. A supplied label is sanitised to `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` (every other character becomes '-', separator runs collapse, leading/trailing separators are trimmed) and truncated to 40 characters, which is what prevents a label from smuggling a path separator or ".." into the filename. Mutating request — subject to the `X-Requested-With` and CSRF-token guards, which reject with 403.

The filename is validated against `^bindery_[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.db$` before any filesystem access, so no slash, backslash or dot other than the `.db` extension can appear — path traversal is rejected with 400 rather than 404. Mutating request — subject to the `X-Requested-With` and CSRF-token guards, which reject with 403.

post.summary: Overwrite the live database with a stored backup
post.description:
`BackupHandler.Restore` (internal/api/backup.go). DESTRUCTIVE side effect: byte-copies `<dataDir>/backups/<filename>` over the live database file and fsyncs it, discarding current data. The server is NOT restarted — the success message tells the operator to restart it, and until they do the running process still holds the old database open.

Two guards run before anything is touched: the filename must match `^bindery_[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.db$` (path traversal rejected with 400), and the request must carry the header `X-Confirm-Restore: true` — any other value, or its absence, is a 400. There is no request body. Mutating request — also subject to the `X-Requested-With` and CSRF-token guards, which reject with 403.

parameters.description: Must be exactly the string "true". Any other value (or omission) is rejected with 400 before the database is touched.

get.description:
Returns a paginated page of books wrapped in `{items,total,limit,offset}`.

Three mutually exclusive code paths are selected by the query string:

1. `authorId` set — loads that author's whole catalogue from the repo and slices it in memory. Only `includeExcluded`, `limit` and `offset` are honoured; `search`, `status`, `mediaType`, `monitored`, `sort`, `releaseFrom` and `releaseBefore` are ignored.
2. `includeExcluded=true` (without `authorId`) — loads the whole set (optionally narrowed by `status`) including excluded books and slices it in memory. `search`/`mediaType`/`monitored`/`sort`/`releaseFrom`/`releaseBefore` are ignored.
3. Default — SQL-paginated with `search`, `status`, `mediaType`, `monitored`, `sort`, `releaseFrom` and `releaseBefore` applied server side.

Results are scoped to the caller's library: admins, API-key callers and installs without tenancy see the shared library, non-admins see only their own plus unowned books. Each returned book has its description HTML-cleaned and its `imageUrl` rewritten to point at the local image proxy (`/api/v1/images?url=…`). Read-only — no side effects.

parameters.name: authorId
parameters.description: Restrict to one author's catalogue. Parsed with strconv.ParseInt; an unparseable value is silently treated as author 0. Selects the in-memory pagination path.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Restrict to books with this status. On the default path `wanted` additionally requires `monitored=true`.

parameters.name: includeExcluded
parameters.description: Include books flagged `excluded`. Only the literal string `true` enables it; any other value (including `1`) is treated as false.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on book title OR author name. Trimmed. Default path only.

parameters.name: mediaType
parameters.description: `ebook` matches ebook/both/unset (mirroring the UI default); `audiobook` matches audiobook/both. Any other value disables the filter. Default path only.

parameters.name: monitored
parameters.description: Tri-state: `true`/`false` pin the monitored flag, anything else (including omitted) means "all". Default path only.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Whitelisted sort key. Unknown values fall back to `title-az`. Default path only.

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on `releaseDate` (ISO-8601 date, lexically compared). Books with a NULL release date are excluded when either bound is set. Default path only.

parameters.name: releaseBefore
parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on `releaseDate` (ISO-8601 date). Default path only.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Non-numeric or non-positive values fall back to the default; values above 500 are clamped to 500.

parameters.description: Row offset. Non-numeric or negative values fall back to 0.

post.summary: Apply a bulk action to many books
post.description:
Applies one action to every book ID in `ids` and returns a per-ID result map. The response is always 200 once the request body validates: individual failures are reported per ID in `results`, not as an HTTP error.

Actions and their side effects:

- `monitor` / `unmonitor` — flip the monitored flag.
- `delete` — delete the book row (database only; on-disk files are not touched by this path).
- `search` — ownership-checked per book, then an asynchronous indexer search is fanned out under a bounded worker pool **after** the response is written. Each requested ID returns `ok:true` immediately; the outcome is only visible in History. Books the caller does not own return a per-ID error.
- `set_media_type` — requires `mediaType`; also re-evaluates each book's wanted/imported status.
- `exclude` — marks each book excluded (bulk callers only ever exclude; un-excluding is the per-book toggle endpoint).

200.description: Per-ID results. Every requested ID has an entry.

400.description: Undecodable body, empty `ids`, unknown `action`, or a `set_media_type` request with an invalid `mediaType`.

401.description: Not authenticated, or the CSRF / X-Requested-With guard rejected the request.

get.summary: Look up a single book by ISBN or ASIN
get.description:
Resolves one book from the external metadata aggregator by a stable identifier. `asin` takes precedence when both are supplied; `isbn` is the original behaviour and the route is shared so existing callers keep working.

The ASIN branch canonicalises the identifier against the primary metadata provider, so the returned record carries the canonical `foreignBookId` — the handler then re-stamps `asin` (when the resolved record lost it) and forces `mediaType` to `audiobook` so the Add Book modal renders the audiobook edition the user searched for.

Calls an external provider (OpenLibrary / Google Books / Hardcover / Audnex); nothing is persisted. Provider transport failures are reported as 502 with a deliberately generic message — the underlying error is only logged server-side because it can embed the provider URL including the Google Books API key.

parameters.name: asin
parameters.description: Audible/audiobook ASIN. Trimmed. Takes precedence over `isbn`.

parameters.name: isbn
parameters.description: ISBN-10 or ISBN-13. Used only when `asin` is absent or blank.

200.description: The resolved book (a transient provider record, not a stored library row: `id` is 0 and `authorId` is unset).

400.description: Neither `isbn` nor `asin` was supplied.

401.description: Not authenticated, or the CSRF / X-Requested-With guard rejected the request.

404.description: No provider record matched that identifier.

502.description: The upstream metadata provider failed or was unreachable.

parameters.description: Book ID (chi URL param parsed with strconv.ParseInt, 64-bit).

get.description:
Returns a single book. The `imageUrl` is rewritten to the local image proxy, the description is HTML-cleaned, and `bookFiles` is populated from the `book_files` table so the frontend can show every tracked on-disk file.

A book owned by another user returns 404 rather than 403, so a non-owner cannot probe for existence (cross-user IDOR guard).

401.description: Not authenticated, or the CSRF / X-Requested-With guard rejected the request.

put.description:
Partial update — every field is a pointer, so only the keys present in the body are applied.

`filePath` is deliberately NOT accepted: it is written by the importer once a grab lands, and letting clients set it arbitrarily would let a caller redirect the on-disk delete performed by `DELETE /book/{id}?deleteFiles=true` or `DELETE /book/{id}/file`.

Manual metadata edits (`title`, `description`, `genres`, `language`, `releaseDate`) additionally **lock** that field, so subsequent metadata refresh / enrichment / merge passes leave it alone. Sending `lockedFields` replaces the lock set wholesale — that is the unlock path. Setting `title` also overwrites `sortTitle`; `genres` entries are trimmed and blanks dropped.

Side effects: changing `mediaType` without also sending `status` re-evaluates the wanted/imported boundary (widening an audiobook to `both` flips it back to `wanted` so the missing ebook is grabbed). When the book transitions **into** `wanted` and is monitored, an indexer search-and-grab is spawned in the background on a shutdown-aware context, unless the global `autoGrab.enabled` setting is `false`.

401.description: Not authenticated, or the CSRF / X-Requested-With guard rejected the request.

404.description: No such book, or the book belongs to another user.

500.description: The update failed to persist.

delete.description:
Deletes the book row. Returns 204 with an empty body.

With `?deleteFiles=true` it first removes every on-disk file tracked in `book_files`. Each path is run through the library-root containment check, so a tampered or mis-imported path outside every configured root cannot redirect the delete — skipped paths are WARN-logged and the database delete still proceeds. Books predating the `book_files` migration fall back to the legacy `ebookFilePath` / `audiobookFilePath` / `filePath` columns. Pending and completed download records for the book are also cleaned up so the queue does not show stale entries.

Ownership is checked before any destructive work; a book owned by another user returns 404.

post.summary: Enrich an audiobook from its ASIN
post.description:
Fetches Audnex data for the book's ASIN and writes narrator, duration, cover image and description onto the record. Requires the book to be `mediaType` `audiobook` or `both` **and** to already have an `asin` set.

After the Audnex fetch it also attempts an ASIN → canonical-provider identity map: if the primary provider resolves the ASIN to a work whose foreign ID is not already claimed by a different book row, and the credited author matches the book's current author, the book's metadata identity is swapped to that canonical record (preserving id, author, status, monitored flag, file paths, media type, narrator, duration, ASIN, calibre id, created timestamp and excluded flag, and falling back to the previous description/cover when the canonical record has none). The map is best-effort and silently skipped on any mismatch or lookup error.

The enriched book is then persisted. Takes no request body.

put.description:
Flips `excluded` to the opposite of its current value and persists it. This is a pure toggle — it takes no request body and there is no way to request a specific value (the bulk `exclude` action is the set-only counterpart). Excluded books are hidden from the default list views unless `includeExcluded=true` is passed.

The returned book carries the new flag and a cleaned description, but is otherwise the pre-toggle in-memory record (no re-read, no image proxying, no `bookFiles`).
