get.description:
Streams the book's content for browser download. **The response is binary, not JSON.**

- Ebook (the resolved path is a regular file): streamed with `http.ServeFile`, so the media type is sniffed from the file itself (`application/epub+zip`, `application/pdf`, …) and `Content-Length` plus a byte-range capable response is provided. `Content-Disposition` is an RFC 6266 / RFC 5987 attachment header carrying both an ASCII-sanitised `filename=` fallback and a percent-encoded UTF-8 `filename*=`.
- Audiobook (the resolved path is a directory): the folder is zipped on the fly and streamed as `application/zip`, so multi-part m4b/mp3 plus cover art come down as one bundle. Zip entry names always use forward slashes.

Path resolution: with `?format` the matching per-format column is used, falling back to the legacy `filePath` only when its on-disk shape matches the requested format (a directory is an audiobook, a regular file is an ebook). Without `?format` the legacy `filePath` wins, then `ebookFilePath`, then `audiobookFilePath`.

Defence in depth: the resolved path must fall under a configured library root (static `LibraryDir`/`AudiobookDir` plus any user-configured root folders resolved at request time). The check fails **closed** — with no roots configured nothing is served. This route is also reached by OPDS reader clients, hence the 404-not-403 response for cross-user access.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Scope the download to one format on dual-format books. Omitted uses the legacy resolution chain. Any value other than `ebook`/`audiobook` is a 400.

200.description: The file. Ebooks stream with their sniffed content type; audiobook folders stream as a zip archive.

Content-Disposition.description: RFC 6266 attachment header. Ebooks carry both `filename=` (ASCII fallback) and `filename*=UTF-8''…`; zipped audiobooks carry `filename="<folder>.zip"`.

schema.description: Zip bundle of the audiobook directory.

400.description: `id` is not an integer, or `format` is neither `ebook` nor `audiobook`.

401.description: Not authenticated, or the CSRF / X-Requested-With guard rejected the request.

403.description: The stored path is outside every configured library root (or no roots are configured — the check fails closed).

404.description: No such book, the book belongs to another user, no file is recorded for the requested format, or the recorded path does not exist on disk.

delete.summary: Delete or deregister a book's file(s)
delete.description:
Two modes.

**Deregister mode** (`?path=<tracked path>`): drops exactly that one `book_files` row and touches nothing on disk. The path must already be tracked against this book — compared after `filepath.Clean` so a copied path with a trailing slash still matches, then deleted by its exact stored spelling. Used to prune a stale row from a book that still has a valid file (e.g. after an ABS library reorganisation moved the file and the importer appended the new path). A history event is written flagged `deregistered:true`.

**Delete mode** (default): removes the on-disk file(s) backing the book and flips its status back to `wanted` so it re-appears on the Wanted page. Files are enumerated from `book_files`, optionally narrowed by `?format`; books predating that migration fall back to the legacy path columns. Deleting a single file also sweeps same-stem siblings in the parent directory (dual-format downloads land epub + mobi in one folder), scoped to the requested format so removing the ebook does not destroy the audiobook. Audiobook paths are directories and are removed by a scoped recursive walk. Paths failing the library-root containment check are skipped with a WARN log, but their `book_files` row is still deregistered so an orphaned path stops surfacing. A `bookFileDeleted` history event records the paths actually removed.

Both modes return the reloaded book with `bookFiles` reattached.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Switches to deregister mode: drop this one tracked `book_files` row without touching the filesystem. Takes precedence over `format`.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Scope the on-disk deletion to one format. Omitted deletes every file for the book.

200.description: The reloaded book, with refreshed status and `bookFiles`.

400.description: `id` is not an integer, or the book has no file to delete for the requested scope.

401.description: Not authenticated, or the CSRF / X-Requested-With guard rejected the request.

404.description: No such book, the book belongs to another user, or (deregister mode) the supplied `path` is not tracked against this book.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Book ID.

post.summary: Rebind a book to a different metadata record
post.description:
Re-points a book at a different upstream metadata record — the fix for a book bound to the wrong work. Fetches the record from the named provider and overwrites the book's metadata identity with it.

Guards: the provider must be `openlibrary` or `hardcover` (lowercased and trimmed before validation), both `provider` and `foreign_id` are required, and if the upstream record credits a different author than the book's current one the call is rejected with 409 unless `force:true` is passed — this stops a typo in the foreign ID silently corrupting authorship.

On success: manual field locks are cleared (a rebind is an explicit "take the new provider's metadata wholesale"), `foreignBookId` and `metadataProvider` are replaced, and title/sortTitle/originalTitle/description/imageUrl/releaseDate/genres/averageRating/ratingsCount/language are overwritten from upstream where non-empty. `lastMetadataRefreshAt` is stamped. User- and importer-managed fields (status, monitored, file paths, media type, ASIN, narrator, calibre id) are preserved.

Further side effects: Hardcover editions are hydrated when the provider is Hardcover; **all** existing series links for the book are removed and re-created from the upstream record's series refs (missing series rows are created); and a `bookRebound` history event records the old and new provider/foreign-ID pair so the operation is reversible by hand.

200.description: The rebound book, with `bookFiles` attached and its image URL proxied.

400.description: `id` is not an integer, the body is undecodable, `provider` or `foreign_id` is blank, or `provider` is not `openlibrary`/`hardcover`.

401.description: Not authenticated, or the CSRF / X-Requested-With guard rejected the request.

404.description: No such book, the book belongs to another user, or the provider has no record for that foreign ID.

409.description: Author mismatch (retry with `force:true`), or a different book row already uses that foreign ID (UNIQUE constraint — this variant carries only `error`).

424.description: No metadata aggregator is configured on this server (`http.StatusFailedDependency`).

500.description: Persisting the rebound book failed.

502.description: Fetching the record from the upstream provider failed. The body carries the upstream error text.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Book ID.

post.summary: Interactively search all indexers for a book
post.description:
Runs a synchronous interactive search across every configured indexer and returns the scored, annotated candidate releases. **Nothing is grabbed** — this only queries.

Search criteria are built from the book plus its author: author name, author aliases, allowed languages from the author's metadata profile, the release year, the ASIN, and the ISBN derived from the book's editions. For dual-format books (`mediaType: both`) two searches run concurrently — one per format, so each uses its own newznab category tree (7xxx ebooks, 3xxx audiobooks) — and the results are merged and deduped; a single `both` search would silently drop all audiobook results.

Results are then filtered by language (author profile takes precedence over the global `search.preferredLanguage` setting) and run through the decision engine, which annotates each release with `approved` / `rejection` using the blocklist, an already-imported check, and the author's quality profile's allowed formats.

Security: the signed indexer download URL is redacted out of every result (`nzbUrl`), because interactive search is available to non-admins and the URL embeds the shared indexer API key — the grab endpoint re-signs it server-side from the indexer ID.

Side effect: the debug payload is cached per caller so the UI can re-fetch it after a reload without re-running the search. Takes no request body.

200.description: Scored candidate releases plus the search audit trail.

400.description: `id` is not an integer.

401.description: Not authenticated, or the CSRF / X-Requested-With guard rejected the request.

404.description: No such book, or the book belongs to another user.

500.description: Listing the configured indexers failed.

post.summary: Start a Calibre library import job
post.description:
Kicks off a background import of the Calibre library at `calibre.library_path` into Bindery (creates/links authors, books, editions and series memberships, and records a rollback-capable run row).

Job contract: this is the **start** half of a start/poll pair. It takes no request body, returns **202 Accepted** immediately with the initial `CalibreImportProgress` snapshot (`running: true`, `message: "opening library…"`), and the caller then polls `GET /api/v1/calibre/import/status` until `running` is `false` and `finishedAt` is set. Only **one import runs at a time** — starting a second while one is in flight returns **409 Conflict** (`calibre import already running`).

Preconditions checked before the job starts (both 400): `calibre.library_import_enabled` must be true, and `calibre.library_path` must be non-empty. The worker goroutine runs on a `context.WithoutCancel` copy of the request context so it survives the HTTP response and can stamp `calibre.last_import_at` on completion.

Side effects: walks the Calibre `metadata.db`, upserts authors/books/editions/series rows, writes a `calibre_import_runs` row plus per-entity snapshots and provenance links (used by the rollback endpoints), and updates the `calibre.last_import_at` setting.

202.description: Import accepted and started. Body is the initial progress snapshot.

400.description: Calibre library import is disabled, or `calibre.library_path` is empty.

409.description: An import is already running (`calibre import already running`).

500.description: The importer refused to start for an unexpected reason.

get.description:
Cheap, stateless poll for the **current or most recent** Calibre import. The importer keeps progress in memory behind a mutex and hands back a fresh snapshot on every call; nothing is mutated.

State machine: `running: false` with a zero `startedAt` means no import has run in this process; `running: true` means one is in flight (`processed`/`total` drive the progress bar); `running: false` with a non-null `finishedAt` means the last run finished — `stats` is populated on success, `error` is non-empty on failure. Progress is process-local and resets on restart.

Returns the persisted Calibre import run history (newest first) — the durable record of past import jobs, as opposed to the in-memory `/calibre/import/status` snapshot. Each run carries its status (`running`, `completed`, `failed`, `rolled_back`) and a `summaryJson` blob with the run's counts.

Returns an empty array when the importer was built without run tracking. Read-only.

Executes the rollback plan for a run: deletes entities the run created, restores the pre-run field values of entities it updated, and unlinks provenance/series rows. **Destructive** — it can remove authors and books wholesale, which is why the whole `/calibre/runs` subtree is admin-only.

On success the result has `preview: false`, `applied: true` and `status: "rolled_back"`, and the run row's status is updated to `rolled_back`. Rollback is metadata-only: files on disk are left untouched and `filesOnDiskWarning` says so when relevant. Takes no request body.

post.description:
Kicks off the "Push all to Calibre" background job: every book with status `imported` and a resolvable file path is POSTed one-by-one to the Bindery Bridge Calibre plugin, and the returned Calibre id is written back onto the book row.

Only **one sync runs at a time** — a concurrent start returns **409 Conflict** (`calibre sync already running`).

The worker runs on `context.WithoutCancel` so the HTTP response-send does not abort a half-finished push. Per-book failures are counted in `stats.failed` and sampled into `errors` (capped at 50 entries); plugin 409 responses count as `alreadyInCalibre` and are treated as success.

400.description: `calibre.mode` is not `plugin`, or `calibre.plugin_url` is empty.

409.description: A sync is already running (`calibre sync already running`).

500.description: The syncer refused to start for an unexpected reason.

get.description: Cheap, stateless poll for the current or most recent Calibre bulk push. `running: false` with a zero `startedAt` means nothing has been run in this process; `running: false` with a non-null `finishedAt` means the last run is complete. `stats` carries the running totals and `errors` a bounded sample (max 50) of per-book failures — `stats.failed` always holds the true failure count. A missing `plugin_url` is a 400; an unreachable plugin is a 502, and a timeout against a LAN address is annotated with a hint that a VPN killswitch may be dropping LAN traffic.
- `mode=off`/`calibredb`: validates that `calibre.library_path` exists and is a directory and that `calibre.binary_path` (when set) is an executable file, then shells out to `calibredb` and returns its version (`message: "calibredb reachable"`).

The probe force-enables the integration for its duration, so it works before `calibre.enabled` has been saved. Read-only: no settings are written.

Because nothing sensitive leaves the process, this route is **not** admin-gated — unlike the PUT and the test probe.

put.description:
Writes the supplied `grimmory.*` settings. Every field is a pointer in Go, so **omitted fields are left unchanged** — this is a partial update, not a replace.

Field semantics:
- `baseUrl` is run through a secure-URL validator; a rejected URL is a 400 and nothing is written.
- `apiKey` is normalized; a normalization failure is a 400. An empty normalized value is ignored (leaves the stored key intact).
- `password` is write-only: a non-empty value replaces the stored one, an empty string means "leave unchanged", so the settings form can round-trip without wiping credentials.
- `enabled` and `username` are written as given (username trimmed).

Individual setting writes that fail are logged and swallowed. The response is the freshly re-read, redacted config — the same shape as `GET /grimmory/config`.

400.description: Malformed JSON body, an invalid/insecure `baseUrl`, or an unusable `apiKey`.

post.summary: Start a bulk push of the library into Grimmory
post.description:
Kicks off the "Push library to Grimmory" background job: every book with status `imported` is uploaded to Grimmory's BookDrop, one upload per file, reusing the shared pusher's client (and its JWT session) plus its idempotency store.

Job contract: no request body; returns **202 Accepted** with the initial status snapshot (`running: true`, `message: "listing imported books…"`), then the caller polls `GET /api/v1/grimmory/sync/status`. Only **one sync runs at a time** — a concurrent start returns **409 Conflict** (`grimmory sync already running`).

Precondition (400): the push config must be *ready* — `grimmory.enabled` true, `grimmory.base_url` set, and at least one of an API key or a username. The handler returns the reason verbatim ("Grimmory integration is disabled", "Grimmory server URL is not configured", "Grimmory credentials are not configured — set a username/password (or API token)").

The worker runs on a `context.WithoutCancel` copy of the request context; when the background-jobs group is wired it is instead tracked on the shutdown-scoped context so SIGTERM cancels and drains it before the database closes (BookDrop has no server-side dedup, so a sync killed mid-upload would re-push everything). Files recorded by a previous push are skipped and counted as `alreadyPushed`; per-book failures are sampled into `errors` (max 50) with the full count in `stats.failed`.

202.description: Sync accepted and started. Body is the initial status snapshot.

400.description: The Grimmory push configuration is not ready (disabled, no base URL, or no credentials).

409.description: A sync is already running (`grimmory sync already running`).

500.description: The syncer refused to start for an unexpected reason.

get.description: Cheap poll for the current or most recent Grimmory bulk push. The body is the in-memory `SyncProgress` (`running: false` + zero `startedAt` = nothing has run this process; `running: false` + non-null `finishedAt` = the last run is complete) **flattened together with** cumulative push state read from the `grimmory_pushes` table: `totalPushedFiles` and `lastPushedAt`. The aggregate is best-effort — if the lookup errors, those two fields are simply omitted/zero and the poll still succeeds.

200.description: Current sync progress plus cumulative push totals.

Connection test for the Grimmory settings page. Any field supplied in the body overrides the corresponding stored setting for this probe only — nothing is persisted. A malformed body is silently ignored (decode errors are discarded), so the request body is effectively optional and an empty probe tests the saved settings.

The probe pings the server for its version, and — when credentials are available — performs a **real login** so a green result proves the push pipeline can authenticate, not merely that the host answers. With no credentials configured the probe still succeeds but the message warns that pushes will fail.

Note that the failure responses use the same `GrimmoryTestResponse` envelope (`ok: false` plus a message), not the generic error shape.

get.summary: Serve an external image through the local cache
get.description:
Caching image proxy for external cover art. **Returns image bytes, not JSON.**

On a cache hit within the 30-day TTL the bytes are served straight from `<dataDir>/image-cache/<first-2-hex>/<sha256(url)>` with the stored content type (defaulting to `image/jpeg`) — no outbound traffic and no third-party tracking. On a miss the image is fetched upstream with a 15-second timeout, validated, written to the cache via a unique temp file plus atomic rename (so concurrent requests for the same URL cannot clobber each other), and returned. Cache writes are best-effort; a write failure is not fatal.

SSRF is blocked in depth: the URL is validated under the strict outbound policy before the fetch, redirects are re-validated and capped at 5, and on the direct (non-proxied) path the dialer re-validates each connection to close the DNS-rebind window. Only `image/*` upstream responses are accepted and the body is capped at 10 MB.

Both cache paths set `Cache-Control: public, max-age=2592000`. Error bodies on this route come from `http.Error`, so they are **plain text**, not the JSON error envelope used elsewhere.

Rows are additionally enriched, best-effort, with a `book` projection (a failed book lookup is logged and the queue still renders).

On a downloader failure it persists the error on the row, writes a `downloadFailed` history event and fires the `downloadFailed` notifier event.

- The scanner recorded an `import_path` that still resolves inside a library root and exists on disk: the files are imported directly, in the background, against the newly assigned book (`{"imported": true}`).
- No usable recorded path but a download client still owns the row: the import retry is reset so the next poll re-derives the location and re-imports (`{"imported": false, "retryQueued": <bool>}`).

Unlike the Calibre and Grimmory jobs there is **no status endpoint and no already-running guard** — repeated calls simply start additional runs, and a failure is only visible in the server log. 1. Ownership-checks the recommendation (404 on mismatch, same anti-enumeration reasoning as dismiss).
2. Rejects with **409** if a book with the same foreign id already exists.
3. Resolves the author — the recommendation's `authorId` if present, otherwise an existing author matched by exact name; if neither resolves, **400**.
4. Creates the book with `status: "wanted"` and `monitored: true`, deriving the metadata provider from the foreign id.
5. Hydrates Hardcover editions for the new book when edition wiring is configured.
6. Runs the new-wanted-book handling that looks for the file already on disk.
7. Dismisses the source recommendation (failures ignored).
8. Unless the file was already found on disk, launches a background search-and-grab on the **process-lifecycle** context so it outlives the request.

Returns **201 Created** with the newly created book.

Fills in a series. Side effects are substantial.

With no book selector in the body (the default), and when the enhanced Hardcover API is enabled, the handler first expands the Hardcover catalogue for the linked series: every catalogue volume missing locally is created as a new book (creating or matching its author, applying the series genre override and locking `genres` when one is set, hydrating Hardcover editions and running the new-wanted-book handling). With a book selector (`foreignBookId`, `providerId` and/or `position`), the enhanced Hardcover API is required and exactly one missing catalogue volume is created, queued and searched.

The request body is optional: an empty body is accepted (EOF is tolerated). `mediaType` defaults to `ebook`. The response reports how many books were newly queued.

Returns the schema-less key/value settings table, ordered by key, with every secret key filtered out.

Access split (see the comments on isSecretSetting in internal/api/settings_handler.go): reads — this route and GET /api/v1/setting/{key} — are available to **every authenticated user**, which is exactly why the secret filter exists; writes (PUT) and deletes (DELETE) are behind auth.RequireAdmin.

A key is treated as secret when it is one of the explicit one-offs (`auth.api_key`, `auth.session_secret`, `auth.session_secret_previous`, `auth.mode`, `auth.oidc.providers`, `abs.api_key`, `hardcover.api_token`, `calibre.plugin_api_key`, `grimmory.api_key`) or matches one of the fail-closed patterns: suffix `.api_key`, `.api_token`, `_secret`, `.password`, `_password`, `.client_secret`, substring `_secret_`, or prefix `auth.oidc.`. Secrets are omitted entirely — not masked — so a secret key is indistinguishable from an unset one. Read-only: no side effects.

200.description: All non-secret settings, ordered by key. Always an array, never null.

500.description: Database error.

get.description:
Returns a single settings row. Readable by **any authenticated user** (the read half of the settings access split); the write half — PUT/DELETE on this same path — is admin-only.

The secret check runs before the lookup: a key classified as secret by isSecretSetting returns the same 404 `setting not found` as a key that does not exist, so this endpoint can never be used to read a credential. Read-only: no side effects.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Settings key, e.g. `import.mode`, `default.media_type`, `search.interval`. Free-form: the table is schema-less, so any key that was written can be read back.

404.description: No such key, or the key is a secret and is therefore hidden from reads (`setting not found` in both cases).

500.description: Database error.

put.description:
Upserts a key/value pair (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE) and stamps `updated_at` with the current UTC time. **Admin-only** — the mutating half of the settings access split, unlike the GET routes which any authenticated user may call.

Secret keys are rejected with 403 unless they are write-only-allowed: only `hardcover.api_token` and `calibre.plugin_api_key` may be written through this generic endpoint (they have no dedicated handler); `abs.api_key` and `grimmory.api_key` are deliberately excluded because their own connection-test handlers persist them. Even for a writable secret the response never echoes the value — the body comes back as `{"key": "...", "value": ""}`.

The value is normalised per key (`hardcover.api_token` is run through hardcover.NormalizeAPIToken) and then validated by validateSettingValue. Unlisted keys pass through unchanged — the table stays schema-less. Validated keys and their rules (an empty value always means 'unset' and is accepted): `hardcover.api_token` rejects control characters; `hardcover.enhanced_series_enabled`, `abs.enabled` accept only true/false (case-insensitive); `calibre.library_path` must stat to an existing directory; `calibre.binary_path` must be an existing regular executable file; `cwa.ingest_path` and `import.drop_folder` must be existing directories (these **stat the local filesystem** as a side effect); `import.drop_layout` in {flat, templated}; `import.drop_link_mode` in {copy, hardlink}; `import.drop_pair_gating`, `default.media_type_strict` in {true, false}; `import.drop_pair_gating_timeout_hours` and `author.default_monitor_latest_count` must be positive integers; `import.mode` in {auto, move, copy, hardlink, external}; `calibre.mode` in {off, calibredb, plugin}; `default.media_type` in {ebook, audiobook, both}; `author.default_monitor_mode` in {all, future, latest, none} (series is per-author only); `library.defaultRootFolderId` must be a positive integer; `metadata.primary_provider` in {openlibrary, dnb}; `calibre.push_path_remap` must match the `from:to[,from:to]` grammar; `calibre.plugin_url` must be an http/https URL with a host that passes the outbound SSRF policy (link-local and cloud-metadata addresses are blocked); `abs.base_url` must pass abs.ValidateBaseURLSecure; `search.interval` and `hardcover.sync_interval` must be Go duration strings within [1h, 168h]. Several keys (`search.interval`, `hardcover.sync_interval`) only take effect on restart.

The DELETE is unconditional — rows-affected is not inspected, so removing a key that was never set still returns 204.

`LogHandler.SetLevel` (internal/api/logs.go), mounted admin-only by `registerSystemLogRoutes` (cmd/bindery/sensitive_routes.go:34). Side effect: a GLOBAL, process-wide mutation — it calls `Ring.SetLevel` on the in-memory buffer and, when a DB slog handler is attached, propagates the same level to the database log writer. The change takes effect immediately for all users and is not persisted across restarts.

The level string is parsed leniently: "debug", "warn"/"warning" and "error" map to their slog levels and ANY other non-empty value silently becomes info. The response echoes the level that was actually applied, so a caller should read it back rather than assume its input was honoured. Only an undecodable body or an empty `level` is rejected. Mutating request — subject to the `X-Requested-With` and CSRF-token guards, which reject with 403.

get.description:
`LogHandler.List` (internal/api/logs.go), mounted admin-only by `registerSystemLogRoutes` (cmd/bindery/sensitive_routes.go:31). Returns a JSON array of log entries — this is a paged query, NOT a stream: there is no SSE, chunked tail or websocket on this route.

Two backends: when a persistent `db.LogRepo` is attached the query runs against the log table and every filter applies; when no repo is attached it falls back to the in-memory ring buffer, whose snapshot honours only `level` and `limit` (`component`, `q`, `from`, `to` are silently ignored) and whose entries use the different `LogbufEntry` shape (`time`/`msg`/`attrs` instead of `id`/`ts`/`component`/`message`/`fields`). The response schema is therefore a union of the two.

All filter values are parsed leniently: an unparseable `level`, `limit`, `offset`, `from` or `to` falls back to the default instead of erroring. On the DB-backed path, when neither `from` nor `to` is given the window defaults to the last hour. Admin-only because the log stream is app-wide and carries other users' book/author titles, OIDC usernames and download names.

parameters.description: Minimum severity to include. Anything unrecognised (including "warning", which is accepted as an alias of warn) falls back to info.

parameters.description: Exact component name to filter on. Ignored on the ring-buffer fallback path.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive RFC3339 start timestamp. Unparseable values are ignored. When neither from nor to is supplied the DB-backed path defaults to the last hour. Ignored on the ring-buffer fallback path.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Inclusive RFC3339 end timestamp. Unparseable values are ignored. Ignored on the ring-buffer fallback path.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Full-text search across message and fields. Ignored on the ring-buffer fallback path.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum entries in one page. Values above the ceiling are clamped to it; values <= 0 or unparseable fall back to the default.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Pagination offset. Negative or unparseable values fall back to 0.

200.description: Matching log entries. Database-backed entries use the LogEntry shape; the ring-buffer fallback returns LogbufEntry.

get.summary: Download matching log entries as a plain-text file
get.description:
`LogHandler.Export` (internal/api/logs.go), mounted admin-only by `registerSystemLogRoutes` (cmd/bindery/sensitive_routes.go:32). Accepts exactly the same filter params as listLogs, then STREAMS the matching entries as a plain-text attachment — deliberately `text/plain; charset=utf-8`, not JSON, because the file is meant to be pasted into a GitHub issue. The response sets `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="bindery-logs-<UTC timestamp>.txt"`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Cache-Control: no-store`.

The body is a comment header (`# Bindery log export`, generation time, the filters that were actually applied, the max-entry cap) followed by one line per entry in `<RFC3339 ms> LEVEL [component] message key=value` form, then a footer with the entry count. Every emitted value is run through `httpsec.RedactSecrets` and has newlines escaped, so secrets in logged URLs do not ride along and one entry is always one line.

Streaming details: rows are pulled 1000 at a time and flushed per page (keyset pagination, not OFFSET), capped at 50000 rows — so `limit` here defaults to and is clamped at 50000, not 200/1000. Reaching the cap is reported in the footer, never silently. Because the 200 and headers go out before the first page is queried, a mid-export store failure is reported as an in-band `# export failed after N entries: ...` comment rather than a 5xx.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Minimum severity to include.

parameters.name: component
parameters.description: Exact component name to filter on. Not applied on the ring-buffer fallback path; the header then names it as NOT applied.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive RFC3339 start timestamp. When neither from nor to is given the window defaults to the last hour ending now.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Inclusive RFC3339 end timestamp. Defaults to now, pinned before paging so rows written mid-export cannot enter the result set.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Full-text search across message and fields.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum entries in the exported file. Both the default and the ceiling are the 50000-row export cap. Supplying it changes the footer wording when the cap is hit.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Starting offset for the first page.

200.description: Streamed plain-text log dump, sent as a file attachment.

2026-08-12T14:03:22.123Z ERROR [importer] import failed book_id=42 path="/library/a b"

Read-only — no mutation, but the cache-size walk touches the filesystem. Requires authentication; no admin role.

get.summary: Configured storage paths and their health
get.description: `StorageHandler.Get` (internal/api/storage.go). Returns the process-level, read-only storage directories loaded from env/config (download, library, and the optional audiobook / audiobook-download dirs) together with per-directory health from `config.CheckDir` (exists / writable / reason) and whether the download dir and library dir share a filesystem so imports can hard-link instead of copy. The health probe touches the filesystem (stat + a writability probe) on every call. Audiobook rows are omitted from `dirs` when unset, because they fall back to the library / download dir. Admin-only: it reveals server filesystem layout. Editable per-library roots live under /api/v1/rootfolder instead.

post.summary: Bulk action on wanted books
post.description:
Applies one action to many books by id and always answers 200 with a per-id result map, so callers can distinguish partial failures without a second request (bulk selections routinely contain stale ids). Supported actions:

- `search` — loads the books in one query and fans out indexer searches for every owned book through a bounded, paced background pool. Ids the caller does not own report `book not found`.
- `unmonitor` — clears `monitored` on each owned book.
- `blocklist` — skips/blocklists each book.

Ownership is enforced per id under tenancy, and a non-owned id is reported with the same opaque "not found" message as a missing one so callers cannot probe other users' libraries.

200.description: Per-id results; every requested id has an entry.

400.description: Body is not valid JSON, `ids` is empty, or `action` is not one of `search`, `unmonitor`, `blocklist`.

get.description: Returns every book with status `wanted`, scoped to the caller's own plus unowned books under tenancy (unscoped for admins, API-key and single-tenant installs). Book descriptions are sanitised before serialisation. Always returns an array, `[]` when nothing is wanted.

parameters.name: includeExcluded
parameters.description: Set to the literal string `true` to include books flagged as excluded. Any other value (including absent) omits them.

500.description: Database error.

get.description:
Serves the process-wide Prometheus registry via `promhttp.HandlerFor`.

Registered at the chi **router root** with `r.Handle("/metrics", metrics.Handler())` (cmd/bindery/main.go:727) — i.e. **outside** the `/api` and `/api/v1` subtrees, so none of `auth.Middleware`, `auth.RequireXRequestedWith`, or `auth.RequireCSRFToken` apply. It is deliberately unauthenticated: Prometheus scrapes carry no session cookie, and the Bindery API key is intentionally not honoured here either; operators are expected to restrict access with a NetworkPolicy, firewall, or reverse-proxy ACL. `security: []` therefore overrides the document-level security.

The endpoint is read-only (no side effects beyond the scrape counters recorded by `metrics.HTTPMiddleware`, which does wrap this route). Exposed series: `bindery_http_requests_total`, `bindery_http_request_duration_seconds`, `bindery_scheduler_runs_total`, `bindery_scheduler_run_duration_seconds`, `bindery_build_info` (version/commit/date labels, set at startup), plus the standard `go_*` runtime and `process_*` collectors.

200.description: Prometheus text exposition format (`text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8`). OpenMetrics negotiation is not enabled.

schema.description: Prometheus exposition format: one `# HELP` / `# TYPE` pair per metric family followed by samples.
examples:
# HELP bindery_build_info Bindery build metadata. Always 1; the labels carry version/commit/date.
# TYPE bindery_build_info gauge
bindery_build_info{commit="e11987b",date="2025-01-01",version="1.0.0"} 1

500.description: One or more collectors failed during the scrape (promhttp's default `HTTPErrorOnError`). The body is a plain-text error, not the JSON `Error` schema.

get.description:
Serves the OPDS 1.2 root navigation feed (`opdsHandler.Root` -> `opds.Builder.BuildRoot`). The feed holds three navigation entries — Authors (`/opds/authors`), Series (`/opds/series`) and Recently Added (`/opds/recent`, last 50 imported books). Link hrefs are absolute and rebuilt per request from the scheme/host the client used, honouring `X-Forwarded-Proto` / `X-Forwarded-Host` behind a reverse proxy. No database access, no side effects.

Auth: this route is outside `/api` and is guarded by `api.OPDSAuth`, which accepts, in precedence order: auth mode `disabled` (open), a valid `X-Api-Key` header or `?apikey=` query value, mode `local-only` from a trusted RFC1918 address, a valid signed session cookie, or HTTP Basic credentials (realm `Bindery OPDS`) — the credential reading apps such as KOReader / Moon+ Reader / Aldiko speak natively. Anything else gets 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Bindery OPDS"`.

200.description: OPDS navigation feed as Atom XML, written with an XML declaration and two-space indentation.

401.description: No accepted credential. JSON body `{"error":"unauthorized"}` plus a Basic challenge header so OPDS readers re-prompt and retry.

429.description: Basic-auth rate limit tripped for the client IP (`auth.LoginLimiter`). Plain-text body via `http.Error`; the Basic challenge header is still sent.

get.summary: Paginated OPDS navigation feed of authors
get.description:
Serves a paginated OPDS navigation feed of every author with at least one imported book (`opdsHandler.Authors` -> `opds.Builder.BuildAuthors`). Authors are sorted case-insensitively by sort name and paged 50 per page; the feed carries OpenSearch `totalResults` / `itemsPerPage` / `startIndex` and `rel="next"` / `rel="previous"` links. For an authenticated non-admin user under tenancy enforcement the feed is scoped to that user's authors (`auth.ListScopeUserID`); API-key, local-only, disabled-auth and admin callers see the whole library. Read-only.

Auth: `api.OPDSAuth` (HTTP Basic, API key by header or `?apikey=`, or session cookie).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number, parsed with `strconv.Atoi`; missing, empty or unparseable values fall back to page 1. Page size is fixed at 50 (`opds.Config.PageSize`). Pages past the end return an entry-less feed.

200.description: OPDS navigation feed of authors as Atom XML.

401.description: No accepted credential; `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Bindery OPDS"` is returned.

429.description: Basic-auth rate limit tripped for the client IP. Plain-text body.

500.description: Author listing or feed build failed (`{"error":"internal server error"}`).

get.summary: OPDS acquisition feed for one author
get.description:
Serves an OPDS acquisition feed of one author's imported books (`opdsHandler.Author` -> `opds.Builder.BuildAuthor`). The path id is parsed with `strconv.ParseInt`; a non-numeric id is rejected with 400 before the builder runs. For a scoped caller, an author they do not own — or one with no books they own — is reported as 404 rather than leaking existence. Read-only.

Auth: `api.OPDSAuth` (HTTP Basic, API key, or session cookie).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Author id (`chi.URLParam` + `strconv.ParseInt`, 64-bit).

200.description: OPDS acquisition feed for the author as Atom XML.

400.description: Path id is not a valid 64-bit integer (`{"error":"invalid id"}`).

401.description: No accepted credential; `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Bindery OPDS"` is returned.

404.description: Author does not exist, or the scoped caller owns none of its books (`opds.ErrNotFound` -> `{"error":"not found"}`). Errors are JSON even though success bodies are Atom XML.

429.description: Basic-auth rate limit tripped for the client IP. Plain-text body.

500.description: Repository or feed-build failure (`{"error":"internal server error"}`).

get.summary: Single-entry OPDS acquisition feed for one book
get.description:
Serves a one-entry OPDS acquisition feed for a single book (`opdsHandler.Book` -> `opds.Builder.BuildBook`) — the publication detail view some clients (Moon+ Reader) open before following the download link. The entry carries the acquisition link to `/opds/book/{id}/file` and a cover link routed through `/opds/images`. For a scoped caller, a book owned by another user surfaces as 404 rather than leaking its metadata. Read-only.

Auth: `api.OPDSAuth` (HTTP Basic, API key by header or `?apikey=`, or session cookie).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Book id (`chi.URLParam` + `strconv.ParseInt`, 64-bit).

200.description: Single-entry OPDS acquisition feed as Atom XML.

400.description: Path id is not a valid 64-bit integer (`{"error":"invalid id"}`).

401.description: No accepted credential; `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Bindery OPDS"` is returned.

404.description: Book does not exist, or the scoped caller does not own it (`{"error":"not found"}`).

429.description: Basic-auth rate limit tripped for the client IP. Plain-text body.

500.description: Repository or feed-build failure (`{"error":"internal server error"}`).

get.summary: Download a book's file over OPDS
get.description:
Streams the book's bytes to the reading app. `opdsHandler.DownloadFile` first re-checks ownership when the caller is scoped (resolves the book and 404s if `owner_user_id` belongs to someone else, closing the direct-URL hole the feeds otherwise filter), then delegates to the shared `FileHandler.Download`, which repeats the ownership check (`auth.CheckOwnership`), verifies the stored path lies under a configured library root, and serves the file with `Content-Disposition: attachment` carrying both an ASCII-folded `filename=` and a UTF-8 `filename*=`. If the resolved path is a directory (an audiobook bundle) it is zipped on the fly and sent as `application/zip`; otherwise the file is served with `http.ServeFile`, so byte-range requests and 206 responses work. Read-only apart from reading from disk.

Auth: `api.OPDSAuth` (HTTP Basic, API key by header or `?apikey=`, or session cookie).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Book id (`chi.URLParam` + `strconv.ParseInt`, 64-bit).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Scopes the download on dual-format books. Omitted: legacy resolution order `file_path` -> `ebook_file_path` -> `audiobook_file_path`. `ebook` / `audiobook` pick that format's path, falling back to the legacy `file_path` only when its on-disk shape matches (regular file = ebook, directory = audiobook). Any other value is a 400.

200.description: The book file. Media type depends on what is stored: a single ebook file is served by `http.ServeFile` (Content-Type sniffed from the extension — epub, mobi, azw3, pdf, …), while an audiobook directory is streamed as a generated zip. `Content-Disposition: attachment` is always set.

206.description: Partial content — `http.ServeFile` honours `Range` requests for single-file downloads (resumable downloads in reading apps).

400.description: Path id is not a valid integer (`{"error":"invalid id"}`) or `format` is neither `ebook` nor `audiobook` (`{"error":"invalid format"}`).

401.description: No accepted credential; `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Bindery OPDS"` is returned.

403.description: The stored path is not under any configured library root, so serving it is refused (`{"error":"access denied"}`).

404.description: Book missing or not owned by the caller (`{"error":"not found"}` / `{"error":"book not found"}`), the book has no file for the requested format (`{"error":"no file available for this book"}`), or the recorded path is absent from disk (`{"error":"file not found on disk"}`).

429.description: Basic-auth rate limit tripped for the client IP. Plain-text body.

500.description: Book lookup failed while enforcing per-user scoping (`{"error":"internal server error"}`).

get.description:
Proxies and caches a cover image so feeds serve covers from this instance instead of hot-linking the metadata provider's CDN (`imageProxyHandler.Serve`, the same handler and the same `<dataDir>/image-cache` as `/api/v1/images`; mounted under `/opds` so it inherits `OPDSAuth` Basic, the only credential a reading app has).

Side effects: on a cache miss it fetches the upstream URL server-side (SSRF-validated first) and writes the bytes plus a `.ct` content-type sidecar into the on-disk cache via a temp file + atomic rename. Responses over 10 MB, non-200 upstreams and non-`image/*` upstream content types are rejected. Cached hits (fresher than the cache TTL) are served straight from disk with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=2592000`.

Auth: `api.OPDSAuth` (HTTP Basic, API key by header or `?apikey=`, or session cookie).

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Absolute upstream image URL. Required — an empty value is a 400. Re-validated against the SSRF policy on every request (a stored value could have been tampered with), and hashed with SHA-256 to derive the cache key.

200.description: The image bytes, with the upstream (or cached) `Content-Type` and a 30-day `Cache-Control`.

400.description: Missing `url` (`url parameter required`) or a URL rejected by the SSRF policy (`invalid url`). Plain-text body via `http.Error`, not JSON.

401.description: No accepted credential; `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Bindery OPDS"` is returned.

429.description: Basic-auth rate limit tripped for the client IP. Plain-text body.

502.description: Upstream fetch failed, returned non-200, returned a non-image content type, or exceeded the 10 MB limit. Plain-text body.

get.summary: OPDS acquisition feed of recently added books
get.description:
Serves an unpaginated OPDS acquisition feed of the 50 most recently updated imported books (`opdsHandler.Recent` -> `opds.Builder.BuildRecent`). Books are sorted by `updated_at` descending with the id as a deterministic tie-break, then truncated to 50. A scoped caller only sees their own books (books with owner 0 remain visible to everyone, matching `auth.CheckOwnership`). Read-only.

Auth: `api.OPDSAuth` (HTTP Basic, API key by header or `?apikey=`, or session cookie).

200.description: OPDS acquisition feed of up to 50 recent books as Atom XML.

401.description: No accepted credential; `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Bindery OPDS"` is returned.

429.description: Basic-auth rate limit tripped for the client IP. Plain-text body.

500.description: Listing imported books failed (`{"error":"internal server error"}`).

get.summary: Paginated OPDS navigation feed of series
get.description:
Serves a paginated OPDS navigation feed of series (`opdsHandler.Series` -> `opds.Builder.BuildSeriesList`), 50 per page, with OpenSearch `totalResults` / `itemsPerPage` / `startIndex` and `rel="next"` / `rel="previous"` links. Scoped to the caller's library for authenticated non-admin users. Read-only.

Auth: `api.OPDSAuth` (HTTP Basic, API key by header or `?apikey=`, or session cookie).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number, parsed with `strconv.Atoi`; missing, empty or unparseable values fall back to page 1. Page size is fixed at 50. Pages past the end return an entry-less feed.

200.description: OPDS navigation feed of series as Atom XML.

401.description: No accepted credential; `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Bindery OPDS"` is returned.

429.description: Basic-auth rate limit tripped for the client IP. Plain-text body.

500.description: Series listing or feed build failed (`{"error":"internal server error"}`).

get.summary: OPDS acquisition feed for one series
get.description:
Serves an OPDS acquisition feed of one series' imported books in series order (`opdsHandler.OneSeries` -> `opds.Builder.BuildSeries`); entry titles are prefixed with the book's position in the series when known. Only books whose status is `imported` and that have a file are included. For a scoped caller with no books in the series the response is 404, so series existence is not leaked by enumeration. Read-only.

Auth: `api.OPDSAuth` (HTTP Basic, API key by header or `?apikey=`, or session cookie).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Series id (`chi.URLParam` + `strconv.ParseInt`, 64-bit).

200.description: OPDS acquisition feed for the series as Atom XML.

400.description: Path id is not a valid 64-bit integer (`{"error":"invalid id"}`).

401.description: No accepted credential; `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Bindery OPDS"` is returned.

404.description: Series does not exist, or the scoped caller owns none of its books (`{"error":"not found"}`).

429.description: Basic-auth rate limit tripped for the client IP. Plain-text body.

500.description: Repository or feed-build failure (`{"error":"internal server error"}`).

get.summary: Serve the embedded SPA and its static assets
get.description:
Catch-all for the embedded frontend. `/` and `/index.html` return the app shell built at startup by `injectBaseHTML` (which prepends `<base href="<URLBase>/">` and the `__bindery_base.js` script tag to `<head>`). Any other path that exists in the embedded `dist` filesystem is served by `http.FileServer` with its own sniffed content type (JS, CSS, fonts, images); every unknown path falls back to the same `index.html` so client-side routes deep-link correctly. HTML responses carry `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate`. No auth middleware is mounted on this route.

Registered in chi as the catch-all `/*`; `{path}` stands in for the wildcard segment, which may contain slashes.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Wildcard remainder of the request path (chi `/*`). Matches an embedded asset, or anything else — unmatched paths fall through to the SPA shell.

200.description: The SPA shell, or an embedded static asset served with its own media type (the listed non-HTML types are representative, not exhaustive).
